children.text: Chapter 1

athāto 'gniṃ praṇeṣyan prāgudak pravaṇam abhyukṣya sthaṇḍilaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ kuryānmadhye prācīṃ rekhām ullikhyodīcīṃ ca saṃhitāṃ paścāt tisro madhye prācyo 'bhyukṣyāgniṃ pratiṣṭhāpayed bhūr bhuvaḥ svar iti lakṣaṇāvṛd eṣā sarvatrāthātaḥ pākayajñān vyākhyāsyāmo huto 'hutaḥ prahutaḥ prāśita iti teṣām ekāgnau homo nitye yajñopavītodakācamane darśapūrṇamāsatantrāḥ svatantrā vā dakṣiṇato 'gneḥ pūrṇapātram upanidadhāti sruvaṃ cāpāṃ pūrṇam uttarato 'gner idhmābarhir devasya tvā savituḥ prasave 'śvinor bāhubhyāṃ pūṣṇo hastābhyāṃ prokṣāmīti prokṣitam upakﾱptaṃ bhavati sakṛd yajuṣā dvistūṣṇīṃ khādiraḥ pālāśo vedhmastadalābhe vibhītakatilvakabādhakanimbarājavṛkṣaśalmalyaraludadhitthakovidāraśleṣmātakavarjaṃ sarvavanaspatīnām idhmaḥ kuśālābhe śūkatṛṇaśaraśīryabalbajamutavanalaśuṇṭhavarjaṃ sarvatṛṇāni śuklāḥ sumanasastāsām alābhe japārūpakākutthābhaṇḍīkuraṇḍakavarjaṃ gandhavatyo vā sarvavarṇāścatasra ājyaprakṛtayo bhavantyūdhanyaṃ vā vāhyaṃ vā dadhi vā payo vā paścād agner ācamanaṃ trir ācāmed dviḥ parimṛjet sakṛd upaspṛśet pādāvabhyukṣya śiraśca śīrṣaṇyān prāṇān upaspṛśed apa upaspṛśya paścād agner upasamāhitasyopaviśya dakṣiṇena pāṇinā bhūmim ārabhya japatīdaṃ bhūmer bhajāmaha idaṃ bhadraṃ sumaṅgalaṃ parā sapatnān bādhasvānyeṣāṃ vinda te dhanam iti vasvantaṃ rātriśced imaṃstomyena tṛcenāgniṃ parisamūhed ādyayā vā triḥ prastaram upasaṃgṛhya pratidiśaṃ paristṛṇāti dakṣiṇapurastād upakramyāgrair mūlāni chādayan paścād vopastīryolaparājibhyām upahared dakṣiṇottaraḥ sandhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now then, when he is about to carry forward the fire, having sprinkled a place sloping eastward or northward, he should make the marked altar-ground: in the middle he draws an eastward line and a joined northward one; afterwards he draws three eastward lines in the middle, sprinkles them, and establishes the fire, saying, "bhūr, bhuvaḥ, svar." This is the rule of marking everywhere. Now then, we shall explain the <s>pākayajñas</s> (cooked domestic offerings): huta, ahuta, prahuta, and prāśita. For these, the oblation is in the single fire, with the regular sacred thread and sipping of water; they follow the procedure of the new- and full-moon rites, or else they are independent. To the south of the fire he places a full vessel, and the sruva filled with water to the north of the fire. With the formula, "At the impulse of the god <s>Savitṛ</s>, with the arms of the <s>Aśvins</s>, with the hands of <s>Pūṣan</s>, I sprinkle you," what has been sprinkled becomes prepared; once with the yajus and twice silently. The fuel may be of khadira or palāśa; in their absence, fuel may be from all forest trees except vibhītaka, tilvaka, bādhaka, nimba, rājavṛkṣa, śalmalī, raluda, dhittha, kovidāra, and śleṣmātaka. In the absence of kuśa grass, all grasses may be used except śūkatṛṇa, śara, śīrya, balbaja, mutavana, and laśuṇṭha. The flowers should be white and pleasant; in their absence, fragrant flowers of every color may be used, except japā, rūpaka, ākuttha, bhaṇḍī, and kuraṇḍaka. There are four basic forms of ājya: what comes from the udder, or what is carried in, or curds, or milk. Behind the fire is the sipping of water: he should sip three times, wipe twice, touch once, sprinkle the feet and the head, and touch the vital breaths located in the head. Having touched water, seated behind the fire with concentration, he touches the earth with his right hand and recites: "This share of the earth we receive; this auspicious, well-omened thing. Drive away the rivals; find the wealth of others for yourself." If it is night, he recites the verse containing "vasu." With the three verses beginning with "imaṃ stomyam," or with the first verse three times, he should sweep around the fire. Taking up the prastara, he spreads it around in each direction, beginning from the southeast, covering the roots with the tips. Or, having spread grass behind, he should bring it near with the two olaparājis; the junction is south-north.

children.text: prastarāt pavitre gṛhṇāti prādeśamātre same apraśīrṇāgre anantargarbhe aṅguṣṭhenopakaniṣṭhikayā ca dhārayann anakhena chinatti pavitre stho vaiṣṇavyāviti trir ūrdhvam adbhir anumārjayed viṣṇor manasā pūte stha iti sakṛd yajuṣā dvistūṣṇīṃ pātrasyopariṣṭāt pavitre dhārayann ājyam āsicyottareṇāgnim aṅgārānnirūhya teṣvadhiśrityāvadyotya darbhataruṇābhyāṃ pratyasya triḥ paryagni kṛtvodagudvāsya pratyūhyāṅgārān udagagrābhyāṃ pavitrābhyāṃ trir utpunātyājyaṃ ca haviśca praṇītāśca sruvaṃ ca devastvā savitotpunātvacchidreṇa pavitreṇa vasoḥ sūryasya raśmibhir iti devo va iti praṇītāḥ punarāhāram ājyasya sakṛd yajuṣā dvistūṣṇīm uttarato 'gneḥ praṇītāḥ praṇīya darbhaiḥ pracchādya dakṣiṇato 'gneḥ prastaraṃ nidhāya prastarasyopariṣṭāt pavitre nidhāya virūpākṣaṃ japaty oṃ tapaśca tejaśca satyaṃ cātmā ca dhṛtiśca dharmaśca sattvaṃ ca tyāgaśca brahmā ca brahma ca tāni prapadye tāni mām avantu bhūr bhuvaḥ svar oṃ mahāntam ātmānam adhyārohāmi virūpākṣo 'si dantājjistasya te śayyā parṇe gṛhā antarikṣe te vimitaṃ hiraṇmayaṃ tad devānāṃ hṛdayānyayasmaye kumbhe antaḥ saṃnihitāni tāni balabhūśca baladhā ca rakṣa ṇo mā pramadaḥ satyaṃ te dvādaśa putrāste tvā saṃvatsare saṃvatsare kāmapreṇa yajñena yājayitvā punar brahmacaryam upayanti tvaṃ devānāṃ brāhmaṇo 'syahaṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ brāhmaṇo vai brāhmaṇam upadhāvati taṃ tvopadhāvāmi japantaṃ mā mā pratijāpsīr juhvantaṃ mā mā pratihauṣīḥ kurvantaṃ mā mā pratikārṣīstvāṃ prapadye tvayā prasūta idaṃ karma kariṣyāmi tanme samṛdhyatāṃ virūpākṣāya dantājjaye brahmaṇaḥ putrāya jyeṣṭhāya śreṣṭhāyāmoghāya karmādhipataye nama iti ||
children.translated_text: From the prastara he takes the two pavitras, each a span long, even, with unbroken tips, and without an inner shoot. Holding them with the thumb and the finger next to the little finger, he cuts them without using the nail. Saying, "You are the two pavitras, belonging to <s>Viṣṇu</s>," he should wipe them upward three times with water; saying, "You are purified by the mind of <s>Viṣṇu</s>," once with the yajus and twice silently. Holding the pavitras above the vessel, he pours in the ājya. Having removed embers north of the fire, placed the vessel upon them, illuminated it, thrown in two young darbha shoots, carried it three times around the fire, set it down to the north, and replaced the embers, he strains the ājya three times with the two pavitras whose tips point northward, along with the oblation, the praṇītā waters, and the sruva, saying: "May the god <s>Savitṛ</s> strain you with an unbroken pavitra, with the rays of the radiant sun." With "devo vaḥ," he deals with the praṇītā waters; the replenishing of the ājya is once with the yajus and twice silently. Having led the praṇītā waters to the north of the fire and covered them with darbhas, having placed the prastara to the south of the fire and the pavitras on top of the prastara, he recites the prayer to <s>Virūpākṣa</s>: "Om. Austerity, splendor, truth, self, firmness, <s>dharma</s>, being, renunciation, <s>Brahmā</s>, and brahman: I resort to these; may they protect me. Bhūr, bhuvaḥ, svar. Om. I ascend the great self. You are <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, Dantājji. Your bed is on a leaf; your houses are in the midspace; your golden measure is there. The hearts of the gods are set within an iron vessel. Guard them, you who are strength and holder of strength. Do not be negligent toward us. Your twelve sons, truly, year after year, having caused you to sacrifice with a desire-fulfilling sacrifice, return again to brahmacarya. You are the brāhmaṇa of the gods; I am the brāhmaṇa of human beings. A brāhmaṇa indeed approaches a brāhmaṇa; I approach you. While I am reciting, do not recite against me; while I am offering, do not make a counter-offering against me; while I am acting, do not act against me. I resort to you. Impelled by you I shall perform this rite; may it be successful for me. Homage to <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, to Dantājjaya, to the son of <s>Brahmā</s>, the eldest, the best, unfailing, the lord of rites."

children.text: sruvaṃ praṇītāsu praṇīya niṣṭapya darbhaiḥ saṃmṛjya sammārgān abhyukṣyāgnāvādhāya dakṣiṇaṃ jānvācyāmedhyaṃ cet kiṃcid ājye 'vapadyeta ghuṇastryambukā makṣikā pipīlikety ā pañcabhya uddhṛtyābhyukṣyotpūya juhuyāt paridhīn paridadhāti madhyamaṃ sthavīyasaṃ paścād dīrghaṃ madhyamaṃ dakṣiṇataḥ kanīyasam uttarataḥ saṃspṛṣṭān dakṣiṇato 'gner apāṃ kośaṃ ninayatyadite 'numanyasvetyanumate 'numanyasveti paścāt sarasvate 'numanyasvetyuttarato deva savitaḥ prasuveti triḥ pradakṣiṇam agniṃ pariṣiñcad deva savitaḥ prasuva yajñaṃ prasuva yajñapatiṃ bhagāya divyo gandharvaḥ ketapūḥ ketaṃ naḥ punātu vācaspatir vācaṃ naḥ svadatviti sakṛd yajuṣā dvistūṣṇīm athedhmam ādāya sruveṇājyaṃ gṛhītvābhighāryāgnāvabhyādadhātyayaṃ ta idhma ātmā jātavedastena vardhasva cedhyasva cenddhi vardhaya cāsmān prajayā paśubhir brahmavarcasenānnādyena samedhaya svāheti manasāghārau juhoti saṃtatam akṣṇayā prajāpataye svāhetyuttaraṃ paridhisandhim anvavahṛtya sruvam indrāya svāheti dakṣiṇaṃ paridhisandhim anvavahṛtyāghārau hutvājyabhāgau juhotyagnaye svāhetyuttarataḥ somāya svāheti dakṣiṇatastāvantareṇāhutiloko bhūḥ svāhā bhuvaḥ svāhā svaḥ svāhā bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ svāhetyagnaye 'gnīṣomābhyām iti paurṇamāsyām agnaya indrāgnibhyām ityamāvāsyāyām uttarapūrvām āhutiṃ juhotyanabhijuhvad āhutyāhutiṃ pratyak sauviṣṭakṛtasthānānnityo 'gniḥ purastāt sviṣṭakṛd ante 'nyatra vapāhomājyahomābhyāṃ na sviṣṭakṛtaṃ pratyabhighārayati sruve sakṛd ājyam upastṛṇāti dvir haviṣo 'vadyati sakṛd ājyenābhighārya pratyabhighārayatyaṅguṣṭhenāṅgulibhyāṃ ca māṃsasaṃhitābhyāṃ dvir haviṣo 'vadyati dvir ājyenābhighārya pratyabhighārayati jāmadagnyānāṃ taddhi pañcāvattaṃ bhavatyaṅgulyā tṛṇakūrcena vā eṣā homāvṛt sarvatra ||
children.translated_text: Having carried the sruva to the praṇītā waters, heated it, wiped it with darbha grass, sprinkled the wiping-grasses, placed them on the fire, and bending the right knee, if anything impure should fall into the ghee, such as a worm, a three-jointed insect, a fly, or an ant, up to five such things, he should remove it, sprinkle it, purify it, and offer. He lays the enclosing sticks: the middle, thicker one behind, the long middle one to the south, the smaller one to the north, all touching. To the south of the fire he pours out a vessel of water, saying, 'O <s>Aditi</s>, give permission'; behind it, 'O <s>Anumati</s>, give permission'; to the north, 'O <s>Sarasvatī</s>, give permission.' Saying, 'God <s>Savitṛ</s>, impel,' he sprinkles around the fire three times clockwise: 'God <s>Savitṛ</s>, impel the sacrifice; impel the lord of sacrifice for a share. May the heavenly <s>Gandharva</s>, purifier of intention, purify our intention; may <s>Vācaspati</s> make our speech pleasing.' He does this once with the sacrificial formula and twice silently. Then, taking up the fuel, taking ghee with the sruva, sprinkling it over, he places it on the fire, saying, 'This fuel is your self, O <s>Jātavedas</s>; by it grow, blaze up, kindle, and increase us with offspring, cattle, brahmanical splendor, and food. Bring us together. Svāhā.' Mentally he offers the two āghāras in an unbroken line, diagonally: 'To <s>Prajāpati</s>, svāhā,' drawing the sruva along the northern joint of the enclosing sticks; 'To <s>Indra</s>, svāhā,' drawing it along the southern joint. Having offered the āghāras, he offers the two shares of ghee: 'To <s>Agni</s>, svāhā,' on the north; 'To <s>Soma</s>, svāhā,' on the south. Between these is the place for oblations. 'Bhūḥ, svāhā; bhuvaḥ, svāhā; svaḥ, svāhā; bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, svāhā.' At the full-moon rite he offers the north-eastern oblation to <s>Agni</s> and <s>Agnīṣomau</s>; at the new-moon rite to <s>Agni</s> and <s>Indrāgnī</s>. Without offering over a previous oblation, oblation after oblation, facing west from the place of the sviṣṭakṛt, the regular fire is in front and the sviṣṭakṛt at the end. Except in the offerings of omentum and ghee, he does not sprinkle back for the sviṣṭakṛt. In the sruva he spreads ghee once, cuts off from the oblation twice, sprinkles once with ghee, and sprinkles back. With thumb and two fingers, where the flesh is joined, he cuts off from the oblation twice, sprinkles twice with ghee, and sprinkles back. For the descendants of <s>Jamadagni</s> this becomes a fivefold cutting. With the finger or with a bunch of grass: this is the procedure for offering everywhere.

children.text: sapavitraṃ prastaram ādatte tasyāgrāṇi sruve 'nakti divyaṅkṣveti madhyam ājye 'ntarikṣe 'ṅkṣveti mūlāni haviṣi pṛthivyām aṅkṣveti prastarāt tṛṇaṃ nirasyatyāyuṣe tveti prastaram agnāvanupraharatyagnaye 'numataye svāheti paścāt tṛṇam anupraharati dviṣantaṃ me 'bhidhehi taṃ caiva pradaha svāheti ghṛtenāktāḥ samidha ādadhāti samṛddhyai svāheti bhūmim ārabhya śīrṣaṇyān prāṇān upaspṛśed apa upaspṛśya dvādaśa prāyaścittāhutīr juhotyākūtyai svāhā
children.translated_text: He takes the prastara grass together with the purifier. He anoints its tips in the sruva, saying, 'In heaven anoint'; its middle in the ghee, saying, 'In the midspace anoint'; its roots in the oblation, saying, 'On earth anoint.' He throws away a blade from the prastara, saying, 'For life, you.' He casts the prastara after it into the fire, saying, 'To <s>Agni</s> and <s>Anumati</s>, svāhā.' Afterwards he casts in the blade of grass, saying, 'Point out my hater; burn him also, svāhā.' He places ghee-anointed fuel-sticks, saying, 'For prosperity, svāhā.' Touching the ground, he should touch the vital breaths in the head; having touched water, he offers twelve expiatory oblations: 'To intention, svāhā.'

children.text: kāmāya svāhā
children.translated_text: 'To desire, svāhā.'

children.text: samṛddhyai svāhā
children.translated_text: 'To prosperity, svāhā.'

children.text: ṛcā stomaṃ samardhaya gāyatreṇa rathaṃtaraṃ bṛhad gāyatravartani svāhā
children.translated_text: 'Make the stoma prosper with the ṛc; the Rathantara with the Gāyatra; the Bṛhat, whose course is Gāyatrī, svāhā.'

children.text: ud u tyaṃ jātavedasaṃ devaṃ vahanti ketavaḥ
children.translated_text: 'The rays carry up that god <s>Jātavedas</s>,'

children.text: dṛśe viśvāya sūryaṃ svāhā
children.translated_text: '<s>Sūrya</s>, for all to behold, svāhā.'

children.text: citraṃ devānām udagād anīkaṃ cakṣur mitrasya varuṇasyāgneḥ
children.translated_text: 'The bright face of the gods has risen, the eye of <s>Mitra</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, and <s>Agni</s>.'

children.text: āprā dyāvāpṛthivī antarikṣaṃ sūrya ātmā jagatastasthuṣaśca svāhā
children.translated_text: '<s>Sūrya</s> has filled heaven, earth, and midspace; he is the self of what moves and what stands, svāhā.'

children.text: ud vayaṃ tamasas pari svaḥ paśyanto jyotir uttaram
children.translated_text: 'Up from beyond the darkness, seeing the higher light,'

children.text: devaṃ devatrā sūryam aganma jyotir uttamaṃ svāhā
children.translated_text: 'we have gone to the divine <s>Sūrya</s> among the gods, to the highest light, svāhā.'

children.text: prajāpate na tvad etānyanyo viśvā jātāni pari tā babhūva
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Prajāpati</s>, no one other than you has encompassed all these created things.'

children.text: yatkāmāste juhumastanno 'stu vayaṃ syāma patayo rayīṇāṃ svāhā
children.translated_text: 'Whatever desires we have as we sacrifice, may that be ours; may we become lords of riches, svāhā.'

children.text: bhūḥ svāhā
children.translated_text: 'Bhūḥ, svāhā.'

children.text: bhuvaḥ svāhā
children.translated_text: 'Bhuvaḥ, svāhā.'

children.text: svaḥ svāhā
children.translated_text: 'Svaḥ, svāhā.'

children.text: bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ svāhetyathāstīrṇān darbhān ānīya praṇītānāṃ ca sruvasya copariṣṭāt kṛtvāpasrāvayañ japati sad asi sanme bhūyāḥ sarvam asi sarvaṃ me bhūyāḥ pūrṇam asi pūrṇaṃ me bhūyā akṣitam asi mā me kṣeṣṭhā iti pratidiśam apa utsiñcati prācyāṃ diśi devā ṛtvijo mārjayantām iti prācīnāvītī dakṣiṇasyāṃ diśi māsāḥ pitaro mārjayantām iti yajñopavītī bhūtvāpa upaspṛśya pratīcyāṃ diśi gṛhāḥ paśavo mārjayantām ityudīcyāṃ diśyāpa oṣadhayo vanaspatayo mārjayantām ityūrdhvāyāṃ diśi yajñaḥ saṃvatsaro yajñapatir mārjayantām iti samudraṃ vaḥ prahiṇomīty apo ninīya samudraṃ vaḥ prahiṇomyakṣitāḥ svāṃ yonim api gacchata
children.translated_text: 'Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, svāhā.' Then, bringing the darbha grasses that had been spread, placing them above the praṇītā waters and the sruva, he lets the water flow off and murmurs: 'You are real; may reality be mine. You are all; may all be mine. You are full; may fullness be mine. You are undecaying; do not perish for me.' He pours out water toward each direction: in the eastern direction, wearing the sacred thread over the right shoulder, 'May the gods, the officiating priests, cleanse'; in the southern direction, 'May the months and the ancestors cleanse.' Then, having become yajñopavītin and touched water, in the western direction, 'May houses and cattle cleanse'; in the northern direction, 'May the waters, herbs, and forest trees cleanse'; in the upward direction, 'May the sacrifice, the year, and the lord of sacrifice cleanse.' Saying, 'I send you to the ocean,' he pours away the waters: 'I send you to the ocean; undecayed, go back to your own womb.'

children.text: ariṣṭā asmākaṃ vīrāḥ santu mā parāseci naḥ svam iti yad apsu te sarasvatītyaṅguṣṭhenopakaniṣṭhikayā cākṣiṇī vimṛjed yad apsu te sarasvati goṣvaśveṣu yanmadhu
children.translated_text: 'May our heroes be unharmed; do not pour away what is ours.' Then with the formula, 'What honey of yours is in the waters, O <s>Sarasvatī</s>, what is in cows and horses,' he should wipe his eyes with his thumb and ring finger.

children.text: tena me vājinīvati mukham aṅdhi sarasvatīti darbhān paridhīṃścāgnāvādhāya vāmadevyena śāntiṃ kṛtvā triḥ paryukṣet sahaviṣkaṃ pradakṣiṇam anvamaṃsthāḥ prāsāvīr iti mantrān saṃnamayet pūrṇapātram upanihitaṃ sā dakṣiṇā yathāśraddhadakṣiṇāḥ pākayajñāḥ pūrṇapātraṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: Having placed the darbha grasses and enclosing sticks on the fire with the words, "With that, O rich-in-prize <s>Sarasvatī</s>, anoint my mouth," he should perform appeasement with the <s>Vāmadevya</s> chant and sprinkle around three times, clockwise, together with the oblation, joining the mantras beginning "You have assented; you have impelled." A full vessel is set down; that is the dakṣiṇā. The pākayajñas have dakṣiṇās according to faith, or else a full vessel.

children.text: puṃsavanaṃ tṛtīye māsyanyatra gṛṣṭer ghṛte caruṃ śrapayitvā pṛṣadājyaṃ vā sthālīpākavat saṃskṛtya puruṣasūktena juhuyānmāṣau ca yavaṃ ca pulliṅgaṃ kṛtvā dadhidrapsenaināṃ prāśayet prajāpatiḥ puruṣaḥ parameṣṭhī sa me putraṃ dadātvāyuṣmantaṃ yaśasvinaṃ saha patyā jīvasūr bhūyāsam iti nyagrodhaśuṅgaṃ phalābhyām upahitaṃ śuklaraktābhyāṃ sūtrābhyāṃ grathitvā kaṇṭhe dhārayed dhruvakumārāyetyācakṣate vāso dakṣiṇā ||
children.translated_text: The puṃsavana is in the third month, before the cow has borne again. Having cooked a caru in ghee, or having prepared pṛṣadājya like a sthālīpāka, he should offer with the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s>. Making a māṣa bean and a barley grain masculine, he should make her eat them with a drop of curds, saying, "<s>Prajāpati</s>, the <s>Puruṣa</s>, the supreme one, may he give me a son, long-lived and renowned; may I become one who bears living sons together with my husband." Having fastened a shoot of the nyagrodha, furnished with two fruits and tied with white and red threads, she should wear it on her neck. They say the mantra is "For a steadfast boy." The dakṣiṇā is a garment.

children.text: athāto nāndīmukhebhyaḥ pitṛbhyaḥ pūrvedyur vyākhyāsyāma āpūryamāṇapakṣe puṇye nakṣatre śvaḥ kariṣyāmīti śvo bhūte vānnaṃ saṃskṛtya śucīn śrotriyān brāhmaṇān anumantrayate śuciḥ śuklam anārdram ācchādya yajñopavītyapa ācamya catuḥśuklān balīn haratī dadhi taṇḍulāḥ surabhi śuklāḥ sumanasa ityagnyāyatane prāgagrān darbhān saṃstīryāgnaye somāya prajāpataye viśvebhyo devebhya ṛṣibhyo bhūtebhyaḥ pitṛbhyaḥ sarvābhyo devatābhyo nama iti haviṣyam annaṃ brāhmaṇebhyaḥ pradāya dadhnā māṣamatsyamāṃsabhakṣyāśanair ityaparam atha catuṣṭayam ādāya vrīhiyavapuṣpasarṣapāṇīti saha tair evodakumbham ādāya manaḥ samādhīyatāṃ prasīdantu bhavanta ityuktvā sapraṇavaṃ nāndīmukhāḥ pitaraḥ prīyantām ityevaṃ yathārtham itare pratibrūyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now then we shall explain the rite for the nāndīmukha ancestors. On the preceding day, in the bright fortnight and under an auspicious asterism, saying, "I shall perform it tomorrow," or when tomorrow has come, he prepares food and invites pure, Veda-learned brahmins. Being pure, clothed in clean white unwet garments, wearing the sacred thread over the left shoulder, and having sipped water, he offers four white bali portions: curds, rice grains, fragrant white flowers, saying, "Homage to <s>Agni</s>, to <s>Soma</s>, to <s>Prajāpati</s>, to all the gods, to the seers, to beings, to the ancestors, to all deities," after spreading darbha grasses with tips to the east in the fire-place. Having given sacrificial food to the brahmins, with foods of curds, māṣa beans, fish, and meat, then taking a group of four things, namely rice, barley, flowers, and mustard seeds, and with those also taking a water-pot, he says, "Let your minds be composed; be gracious." Then, with the praṇava, he says, "May the nāndīmukha ancestors be pleased," and likewise according to the occasion; the others should reply.

children.text: sīmantonnayanaṃ caturthe māsi ṣaṣṭhe 'ṣṭame vā pūrvapakṣe puṇye nakṣatre hastottarābhir vā kuryāt tilamudgamiśraṃ sthālīpākaṃ śrapayitvānvārabdhāyāṃ juhuyānmahāvyāhṛtibhir hutvā prājāpatyayā cāthaināṃ paścād agner bhadrapīṭha upaveśyairakāyāṃ vāhatottarāyāṃ tasyai triḥ śuklayā śalalyā prāṇasaṃmitaṃ sīmantaṃ kuryāc chuklenā mūrdhnaḥ prāṇāya tvāpānāya tvā vyānāya tvetyathāsyā dakṣiṇaṃ keśāntaṃ sragbhir alaṃkṛtya tathottaraṃ hiraṇyavatīnām apāṃ kāṃsyaṃ pūrayitvā tatrainām avekṣayan pṛccheddhiṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ kiṃ paśyasīti parā pratyāha prajāṃ paśūn saubhāgyaṃ mahyaṃ dīrgham āyuḥ patyur iti vāso dakṣiṇā hiraṇyaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: The sīmantonnayana should be performed in the fourth, sixth, or eighth month, in the bright fortnight, under an auspicious asterism, or under Hasta and the Uttarās. Having cooked a sthālīpāka mixed with sesame and mung beans, he should offer while she has touched him; after offering with the great vyāhṛtis and with the verse to <s>Prajāpati</s>, he should then seat her west of the fire on an auspicious stool, or on an uninjured bull-hide with the neck to the north. For her he should part the hair-line three times, to the measure of the breath, with a white porcupine quill, from the head, saying, "For prāṇa you, for apāna you, for vyāna you." Then, having adorned the end of her right hair with garlands, and likewise the left, he should fill a bronze vessel with gold-containing water and, making her look into it, ask, "Hiṃ, bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, what do you see?" She answers in return, "Offspring, cattle, good fortune, long life for myself and for my husband." The dakṣiṇā is a garment, or gold.

children.text: kumāre jāte jātakarma prākstanaprāśanād vrīhiṃ ca yavaṃ ca jātarūpeṇāvaghṛṣyedam annam iti prāśayed idam annam ayaṃ rasa idaṃ prāṇenāmṛtaṃ saha pṛthivī te mātā dyauḥ pitā jīvāhi śaradaḥ śataṃ paśyāhi śaradaḥ śatam ityathainam abhimantrayate 'ṅgādaṅgāt sambhavasi hṛdayād adhi jāyase
children.translated_text: When a boy is born, the jātakarma is performed before he is made to suck the breast. He should rub rice and barley with gold and make him eat it, saying, "This is food." "This is food; this is sap; this is immortality together with breath. Earth is your mother, heaven your father. Live a hundred autumns; see a hundred autumns." Then he addresses him with the mantra, "From limb after limb you arise; from the heart you are born.

children.text: ātmā vai putranāmāsi sa jīva śaradaḥ śataṃ paśyāhi śaradaḥ śatam ityathainaṃ paridadātyahne tvā paridadāmyahastvā rātryai paridadātu rātristvāhorātrābhyāṃ paridadātvahorātrau tvārdhamāsebhyaḥ paridattām ardhamāsāstvā māsebhyaḥ paridadatu māsāstvartubhyaḥ paridadatv ṛtavastvā saṃvatsarāya paridadatu saṃvatsarastvā jarāyai mṛtyave paridadātviti ko 'si katamo 'sītyāha saṃ māsaṃ praviśāsāvityathāsya guhyaṃ nāma dadāti vedo 'sītyathāsya mūrdhānam upajighratyaśmā bhava paraśur bhava hiraṇyam astṛtaṃ bhava paśūnāṃ tvā hiṃkāreṇābhijighrāmītyevam eva pravāsād etya putrāṇāṃ mūrdhānam upajighrati phalīkaraṇamiśrān sarṣapān daśarātram agnau juhuyāt śaṇḍāyeti dvābhyāṃ śaṇḍāya markāyopavīrāya śauṇḍikera ulūkhalo malimluco duṇāśi cyavano naśyatāditaḥ svāhā
children.translated_text: You are indeed the self, bearing the name son; live a hundred autumns; see a hundred autumns." Then he entrusts him: "To day I entrust you; let day entrust you to night; let night entrust you to day and night; let day and night entrust you to the half-months; let the half-months entrust you to the months; let the months entrust you to the seasons; let the seasons entrust you to the year; let the year entrust you to old age and death." He says, "Who are you? Which one are you? Enter the month, O so-and-so." Then he gives him his secret name: "You are the <s>Veda</s>." Then he smells the crown of his head: "Be a stone; be an axe; be unwounded gold. I smell you with the hiṃkāra of cattle." In just this way, after returning from a journey, he smells the heads of his sons. For ten nights he should offer mustard seeds mixed with chaff in the fire with the two verses to <s>Śaṇḍa</s>: "To <s>Śaṇḍa</s>, to <s>Marka</s>, to <s>Upavīra</s>, to the tavern-keeper, to the mortar, to the thief, to the devourer of evil, to <s>Cyavana</s>: perish from here, svāhā.

children.text: ālikhan vilikhann animiṣan kiṃvadanta upaśrutir aryamṇaḥ kumbhī śatruḥ pātrapāṇir nipuṇahāntrīmukhaḥ sarṣapāruṇo naśyatāditaḥ svāheti daśarātraṃ dampatī sūtakau bhavatastasyānte snātvotthānam ||
children.translated_text: To the scratcher, the tearer, the unwinking one, rumor, overhearing, <s>Aryaman</s>'s pot, the enemy, the vessel-handed one, the skilled one, the killer-faced one, and the mustard-red one: perish from here, svāhā." For ten nights the husband and wife remain in birth-impurity; at the end of that, having bathed, there is the rising up.

children.text: athāto nāmakarma pūrvapakṣe puṇye nakṣatre dvādaśyāṃ vā pitā nāma kuryād ācāryo vā tam ahatena vāsasā samanuparigṛhya pitāṅkenāsīta tasya nāmadheyaṃ dadyād dvyakṣaraṃ caturakṣaraṃ vā ghoṣavadādyantarantastham anunakṣatram anudaivatam anunāmātaddhitam ākārāntaṃ stryai yathārthaṃ vā kumārayajñeṣu ca nakṣatraṃ nakṣatradaivataṃ tithim iti yajate 'ṣṭāvanyā juṣṭā devatā yajate 'gnidhanvantariprajāpatim indraṃ vasūn rudrān ādityān viśvān devān ityetāsu sviṣṭāsu sarvā devatā abhīṣṭā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Now then, the naming rite. In the bright fortnight, under an auspicious asterism, or on the twelfth lunar day, the father, or else the ācārya, should give the name. Having wrapped him completely in an unworn garment, the father should sit with him on his lap. He should give him his name: it should be of two syllables or four syllables, beginning with a voiced sound and ending with an internal semivowel, corresponding to the asterism, corresponding to the deity, not a patronymic derivative, and ending in -a; for a girl it should be suitable in meaning. And in the rites for boys he offers with the asterism, the deity of the asterism, and the lunar day. Thus he sacrifices to the eight other favored deities: <s>Agni</s>, <s>Dhanvantari</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s>, <s>Indra</s>, the <s>Vasus</s>, the <s>Rudras</s>, the <s>Ādityas</s>, and all the gods. When these have been duly offered to, all the deities become propitiated.

children.text: athātaḥ prāśanakarma pūrvapakṣe puṇye nakṣatre brāhmaṇān bhojayitvā haviṣyam annaṃ prāśayed annapate 'nnasya no dehyanamīvasya śuṣmiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Now then, the first-feeding rite. In the bright fortnight, under an auspicious asterism, after feeding brāhmaṇas, he should make the child eat sacrificial food, saying, "O lord of food, give us food that is free from disease and full of strength.

children.text: pra pradātāraṃ tāriṣa ūrjaṃ no dhehi dvipade śaṃ catuṣpada iti ||
children.translated_text: Carry the giver forward; place nourishment in us, welfare for the two-footed and for the four-footed."

children.text: tṛtīye saṃvatsare jaṭāḥ kurvīta garbhatṛtīya ityeka udagayane pūrvapakṣe puṇye nakṣatre brāhmaṇān svasti vācyāparāhṇe 'gniṃ praṇayitvā dakṣiṇato 'gneścatvāri pūrṇapātrāṇi nidadhyāt vrīhiyavānām abhito madhye tilamāṣāṇām ācāntodake 'nvārabdhe juhuyānmahāvyāhṛtibhir hutvā virūpākṣeṇātra pañcamīṃ juhoti sarvauṣadhībhiḥ sphāṇṭam udakam ānayanti vrīhiyavāstilamāṣā ityetat sarvauṣadham āyam agāt savitā kṣureṇeti kṣuram ādatta āyam agāt savitā kṣureṇa viśvair devair anumato marudbhiḥ
children.translated_text: In the third year he should arrange the matted locks; some say in the third year from conception. In the sun's northern course, in the bright fortnight, under an auspicious asterism, after having brāhmaṇas pronounce blessings, in the afternoon, having led the fire forward, he should set four full vessels to the south of the fire, filled with rice and barley, and on both sides, in the middle, vessels with sesame and māṣa beans. When he has sipped water and the child has touched him, he should offer; after offering with the great vyāhṛtis, he offers the fifth oblation here with the Virūpākṣa formula. They bring warm water with all herbs; rice, barley, sesame, and māṣa beans are this all-herb mixture. With "<s>Savitṛ</s> has come with the razor," he takes the razor: "<s>Savitṛ</s> has come with the razor, approved by all the gods and by the <s>Maruts</s>.

children.text: sa naḥ śivo bhavatu viśvakarmā yūyaṃ pāta svastibhiḥ sadā na ityuṣṇena vāya udakenehītyudakam ādatta uṣṇena vāya udakenehyaditiḥ keśān vapatvityāpa undantu jīvasa iti dakṣiṇaṃ keśāntam abhyundyād āpa undantu jīvase dīrghāyuṣṭvāya varcasa iti tasmiṃstisro darbhapiñjūlīr upadadhātyekāṃ vā dhārayatu prajāpatir iti dhārayed dhārayatu prajāpatiḥ punaḥ punaḥ suvaptavā ityūrdhvaṃ trir ādarśena spṛṣṭvā yena dhāteti kṣureṇa chindyād yena dhātā bṛhaspater agner indrasya cāyuṣe 'vapat
children.translated_text: May that all-maker be auspicious for us; do you always protect us with blessings." With "Come here with warm water, O <s>Vāyu</s>," he takes the water: "Come here with warm water, O <s>Vāyu</s>; let <s>Aditi</s> shave the hairs." With "Let the waters moisten for life," he moistens the right end of the hair: "Let the waters moisten for life, for long life and brilliance." On it he places three bunches of darbha grass, or one. With "Let <s>Prajāpati</s> hold it," he should hold it: "Let <s>Prajāpati</s> hold it again and again, for good shaving." Having touched it upward three times with a mirror, he cuts it with the razor with the verse beginning "By which <s>Dhātṛ</s>": "By which <s>Dhātṛ</s> shaved for the life of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, <s>Agni</s>, and <s>Indra</s>,

children.translated_text: with that I shave you for long life, for good renown, and for well-being." In this same way, behind and then to the north, with each mantra, he should place the hairs, the bunches of darbha, and the remnants in unfallen bull's dung that has not touched the ground: for a brāhmaṇa in front, for the other two varṇas behind. With "What is with the razor," he gives the razor to the barber: "With the razor, with the blunt shaving instrument with which you shave, O barber, make the limbs pure; do not injure life or brilliance, O barber." According to their gotra rule or family rule, when he has bathed, he should offer expiatory oblations. The rite for a woman should be performed by the same procedure, without mantras; if it is with mantras, he should offer afterwards. Then, taking hold of his head, he recites: "The triple life of <s>Kaśyapa</s>, the triple life of <s>Jamadagni</s>, the triple life that belongs to the gods: let that triple life be yours." He should bury the hairs in a grain-threshing floor or in a cow-pen. The one who brings about welfare should carry away the full vessels. A cow is the dakṣiṇā.

children.text: saptame brāhmaṇam upanayīta pañcame brahmavarcasakāmaṃ navame tvāyuṣkāmam ekādaśe kṣatriyaṃ dvādaśe vaiśyaṃ nāti ṣoḍaśam upanayīta prasṛṣṭavṛṣaṇo hyeṣa vṛṣalībhūto bhavatīti tata enaṃ snātam alaṃkṛtam āktākṣaṃ kṛtanāpitakṛtyam ānayanti tam ahatena vāsasā paridadhīta parīmaṃ someti yathāvarṇaṃ parīmaṃ soma brahmaṇā mahe śrotrāya dadhmasi
children.translated_text: In the seventh year he should initiate a brāhmaṇa; in the fifth if he desires brahmic brilliance; in the ninth if he desires long life. A kṣatriya is initiated in the eleventh, a vaiśya in the twelfth. He should not initiate him later than the sixteenth, for then, with his testicles developed, he becomes as one degraded to a vṛṣalī's status. Then they bring him bathed, adorned, with his eyes anointed, and with the barber's work done. He should clothe him in an unworn garment, saying, "Around this one, O <s>Soma</s>," according to varṇa: "Around this one, O <s>Soma</s>, by brahman we place him for great sacred learning,

children.text: yathemaṃ jarimā ṇayāj jyok śrotre adhi jāgarāj jīvāhi śaradaḥ śataṃ paśyāhi śaradaḥ śatam iti parīmam indra brahmaṇā mahe rāṣṭrāya dadhmasi
children.translated_text: so that old age may lead this one onward, so that he may long keep watch over sacred learning; live a hundred autumns, see a hundred autumns." "Around this one, O <s>Indra</s>, by brahman we place him for great royal power."

children.translated_text: With the words, "As this old age may lead him, may he remain awake long in nourishment; live a hundred autumns; see a hundred autumns," then, having seated him behind the fire facing east and wearing the yajñopavīta, the teacher makes him sip water. When he has sipped, the teacher raises him, spreads darbhas north of the fire with their tips eastward, places an unbroken stone upon them, and there makes him set his right foot on the stone, saying, "Mount this stone; like a stone be firm. Drive away the one who hates you, and may the hater not strike you down." Then, having seated him behind the fire facing east, the teacher, standing to the north and having touched him from behind, should offer oblations. Having offered with the great vyāhṛtis and with the deva-offerings, he puts the saṃpāta into his mouth, with each mantra: "Bhūr, to the ṛcs, svāhā; bhuvaḥ, to the yajuses, svāhā; svaḥ, to the sāmans, svāhā." When it has been eaten and he has sipped water, the teacher raises him and leads him clockwise around the fire with "Homage to <s>Vāta</s>": "Homage to <s>Vāta</s>; homage be to <s>Agni</s>; homage to the earth; homage to the plants; homage to you, the unseen, the great, I make." "Approach, O one who is to receive; give, O giver; give this <s>Veda</s> to so-and-so." Then, having made him stand behind the fire facing east, the teacher stands in front facing west, and the two make hollowed hands. The teacher is to the north; another fills his hands with water, and with what flows out the other man's hands are filled. Then he instructs him: "I have come to brahmacarya; lead me near." "What is your name?" Saying "so-and-so," he gives his name. There the teacher murmurs: "Hiṃ, bhūr bhuvaḥ svar. We have come; we have met. Drive mortal evil far away."

children.text: ariṣṭāḥ saṃcaremahi svasti caratād ayam ityathāsya dakṣiṇena hastena dakṣiṇaṃ hastaṃ gṛhṇātīndraste hastam agrabhīd dhātā hastam agrabhīt pūṣā hastam agrabhīt savitā hastam agrabhīd aryamā hastam agrabhīnmitrastvam asi dharmaṇāgnir ācāryastaveti prāṇānāṃ granthir asīti nābhideśam ārabhya japati prāṇānāṃ granthir asi mā visrasāmṛta mṛtyor antaraṃ kurviti dakṣiṇam aṃsam anvavamṛśya mayi vrata iti hṛdayadeśam ārabhya japati mayi vrate hṛdayaṃ te astu mama cittam anu cittaṃ te astu
children.translated_text: "Unharmed may we move about; may this one go in well-being." Then with his right hand he takes the initiate's right hand: "<s>Indra</s> has grasped your hand; <s>Dhātṛ</s> has grasped your hand; <s>Pūṣan</s> has grasped your hand; <s>Savitṛ</s> has grasped your hand; <s>Aryaman</s> has grasped your hand. You are <s>Mitra</s> by <s>dharma</s>; <s>Agni</s> is your teacher." Saying, "You are the knot of the breaths," he touches the region of the navel and murmurs: "You are the knot of the breaths; do not become loosened. Put immortality between us and death." Having touched his right shoulder, he says, "The vow is in me." Touching the region of the heart he murmurs: "May your heart be in my vow; may your thought follow my thought."

children.text: mama vācam ekavrato juṣasva bṛhaspatistvā niyunaktu mayītyathainaṃ paridadātyagnaye tvā paridadāmi vāyave tvā paridadāmi devāya tvā savitre paridadāmyadbhyastvauṣadhībhyaḥ paridadāmi sarvebhyastvā devebhyaḥ paridadāmi sarvebhyastvā bhūtebhyaḥ paridadāmyariṣṭyā ityathainaṃ saṃśāsti brahmacāryasi samidha ādhehy apo 'śāna karma kuru mā divā svāpsīr ityagnaye samidham āhārṣam iti ghṛtenāktāḥ samidha ādadhātyagnaye samidham āhārṣaṃ bṛhate jātavedase
children.translated_text: "As one under a single vow, accept my speech. May <s>Bṛhaspati</s> appoint you to me." Then he entrusts him: "I entrust you to <s>Agni</s>; I entrust you to <s>Vāyu</s>; I entrust you to the god <s>Savitṛ</s>; I entrust you to the waters and the plants; I entrust you to all the gods; I entrust you to all beings, for safety." Then he instructs him: "You are a brahmacārin; put on fuel-sticks; drink water; do the work; do not sleep by day." With "I have brought a fuel-stick for <s>Agni</s>," he lays down fuel-sticks smeared with ghee: "I have brought a fuel-stick for <s>Agni</s>, for great <s>Jātavedas</s>."

children.text: yathā tvam agne samidhā samidhyasa evam aham āyuṣā varcasā tejasā sanyā medhayā prajñayā prajayā paśubhir brahmavarcasenānnādyena dhanena samedhiṣīya svāhā
children.translated_text: "As you, O <s>Agni</s>, are kindled by the fuel-stick, so may I prosper in life, brilliance, fiery energy, descendants, intelligence, understanding, offspring, cattle, brahmanic splendor, food fit to eat, and wealth. Svāhā."

children.text: apsarāsu yā medhā gandharveṣu ca yanmanaḥ
children.translated_text: "The intelligence that is among the apsarases, and the mind that is among the gandharvas,"

children.text: daivī medhā manuṣyajā sā māṃ medhā surabhir juṣatāṃ svāhā
children.translated_text: "that divine intelligence, born among human beings, may that fragrant intelligence favor me. Svāhā."

children.text: bhūḥ svāhā bhuvaḥ svāhā svaḥ svāhā bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ svāhetīyaṃ duruktād iti mekhalām ābadhnīta iyaṃ duruktāt paribādhamānā varṇaṃ pavitraṃ punatī ma āgāt
children.translated_text: With "Bhūḥ svāhā; bhuvaḥ svāhā; svaḥ svāhā; bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ svāhā," he ties on the mekhalā with the verse beginning "This from ill-spoken speech": "This one, warding off ill-spoken speech, has come to me, purifying the color, the purifier."

children.text: prāṇāpānābhyāṃ balam ābharantī svasā devī subhagā mekhaleyam
children.translated_text: "Bringing strength through prāṇa and apāna, this divine sister, fortunate, is the mekhalā."

children.text: ṛtasya goptrī tapasaḥ paraspī ghnatī rakṣaḥ sahamānā arātīḥ
children.translated_text: "Guardian of ṛta, surpassing austerity, striking down the rakṣas, overcoming enemies."

children.text: sā mā samantād abhiparyehi bhadre bhartāraste mekhale mā riṣāmeti mauñjīṃ brāhmaṇasya maurvīṃ rājanyasya muñjamiśrāṃ tāmalīṃ vaiśyasya mauñjīṃ vā sarveṣām atha paridhānāni kṣaumaṃ vā śāṇaṃ vāntaraṃ brāhmaṇasyaiṇeyam uttaraṃ rauravaṃ rājanyasyājaṃ vaiśyasyaiṇeyaṃ vā sarveṣāṃ svastyayano 'sīti daṇḍaṃ prayacchet prāṇasaṃmitaṃ pālāśaṃ brāhmaṇasya bailvaṃ brahmavarcasakāmasya naiyagrodhaṃ rājanyasyaudumbaraṃ vaiśyasya pālāśaṃ vā sarveṣāṃ mātaraṃ prathamaṃ bhikṣetāthānyāḥ suhṛdo bhavatpūrvayā brāhmaṇo bhikṣeta bhavati bhikṣāṃ dehīti bhavanmadhyamayā rājanyo bhikṣāṃ bhavati dehīti bhavadantyayā vaiśyo dehi bhikṣāṃ bhavatīti kṣāṃ ca hiṃ ca na vardhayed bhavatpūrvayā vā sarve prāyaścittaṃ ced utpadyeta jīvā stha jīvayata metyenam apa ācāmayejjīvā stha jīvayata māpo nāma sthāmṛtā nāma stha svadhā nāma stha tāsāṃ vo bhukṣiṣīya sumatau mā dhatta śivā me bhavata namo vo 'stu mā mā hiṃsiṣṭeti bhaikṣam upanyāhṛtam ūrdhvaṃ trirātrāt sāvitrīṃ prabrūyāt tad ahar vā paścād agneḥ paccho 'rdharcaśaḥ sarvām ityanūcya vedam ārabhyāgne vratapata iti ghṛtenāktāḥ samidha ādadhātyagne vratapate vrataṃ cariṣyāmi tacchakeyaṃ tanme rādhyatāṃ svāhā
children.translated_text: He should give the girdle, saying, "Come around me on every side, auspicious one; O girdle, may my husbands not be harmed." For a brāhmaṇa it is of muñja grass; for a rājanya, of bowstring hemp; for a vaiśya, of tamāla mixed with muñja; or a muñja girdle may be used for all. Next are the garments: for a brāhmaṇa, linen or hemp as the lower garment and antelope skin as the upper; for a rājanya, ruru-deer skin; for a vaiśya, goat skin; or antelope skin may be used for all. Saying, "You are a bringer of well-being," he should give the staff, equal to the breath: for a brāhmaṇa, of palāśa wood; for one desiring brahmanic splendor, of bilva; for a rājanya, of nyagrodha; for a vaiśya, of udumbara; or palāśa may be used for all. He should beg first from his mother and then from other well-wishers. A brāhmaṇa should beg with the word "bhavat" first: "Lady, give alms." A rājanya with "bhavat" in the middle: "Alms, lady, give." A vaiśya with "bhavat" last: "Give alms, lady." He should not lengthen the syllables kṣā and hiṃ. Or all may use the form with "bhavat" first. If an expiation arises, he should make him sip water, saying, "You are living; give life to me. You are living; give me life. You are waters by name, immortal by name, svadhā by name. May I partake of you in your favor; place me in good thought. Be auspicious for me. Homage to you; do not injure me." When the collected alms have been brought near, after three nights, or on that very day, he should teach the Sāvitrī behind the fire, foot by foot, half-verse by half-verse, and then the whole. Having recited it, he begins the Veda and lays down fuel-sticks smeared with ghee, saying, "O <s>Agni</s>, lord of vows, I shall observe the vow. May I be able to do it; may it be accomplished for me. Svāhā."

children.text: vāyo vratapate vrataṃ cariṣyāmi tacchakeyaṃ tanme rādhyatāṃ svāhā
children.translated_text: "O <s>Vāyu</s>, lord of vows, I shall observe the vow. May I be able to do it; may it be accomplished for me. Svāhā."

children.text: āditya vratapate vrataṃ cariṣyāmi tacchakeyaṃ tanme rādhyatāṃ svāhā
children.translated_text: "O <s>Āditya</s>, lord of vows, I shall observe the vow. May I be able to do it; may it be accomplished for me. Svāhā."

children.text: vratānāṃ vratapate vrataṃ cariṣyāmi tacchakeyaṃ tanme rādhyatāṃ svāheti tad etad vratādeśanaṃ sarvatra vratasamāptāvagne vratapate vratam acāriṣaṃ tad aśakaṃ tanme 'rādhi svāheti mantrān saṃnamayed athainaṃ saṃśāsti brahmacāryācāryādhīnaḥ praśānto 'dhaḥśāyī daṇḍamekhalājinajaṭādhārī stryanṛtamadhumāṃsagandhamālyavarjī bhaveti trirātram akṣārālavaṇāśyūrdhvaṃ trirātrāt prācīṃ vodīcīṃ vā diśam upaniṣkramya palāśaṃ gatvā vyāhṛtibhir abhyajya sthālīpākeneṣṭvā yajñopavītaṃ daṇḍam ityudasya pratyeyād gaur dakṣiṇā ||
children.translated_text: "O lord of vows among vows, I shall observe the vow. May I be able to do it; may it be accomplished for me. Svāhā." This is the instruction in the vow. Everywhere at the completion of a vow he should adapt the mantras: "O <s>Agni</s>, lord of vows, I have observed the vow. I was able to do it; it has been accomplished for me. Svāhā." Then he instructs him: "Be a brahmacārin, dependent on the teacher, calm, sleeping on the ground, bearing staff, girdle, antelope skin, and matted hair, avoiding women, falsehood, honey, meat, perfumes, and garlands." For three nights he should eat food without alkali and without salt. After three nights, having gone forth toward the east or north, having gone to a palāśa tree, having anointed himself with the vyāhṛtis, and having sacrificed with a sthālīpāka, he should cast away the sacred thread and the staff and then return. A cow is the dakṣiṇā.

children.text: sāyaṃprātar udakānte pūto bhūtvā sapavitro 'dbhir mārjayetāpohiṣṭhīyābhis tisṛbhis tarat sa mandī dhāvatīti catasṛbhir vāmadevyam ante śucau deśe darbheṣvāsīno darbhān dhārayamāṇaḥ pratyaṅmukho vāgyataḥ saṃdhyāṃ manasā dhyāyed ā nakṣatrāṇām udayād uditeṣu nakṣatreṣu trīn prāṇāyāmān dhārayitvā sāvitrīṃ sahasrakṛtva āvartayecchatakṛtvo vā daśāvaram athāgnim upatiṣṭhate 'gne tvaṃ no antama ityatha varuṇam upatiṣṭhate tvaṃ varuṇa uta mitra ityetayaivāvṛtā prātaḥ prāṅmukhastiṣṭhann athādityam upatiṣṭhata ud vayaṃ tamasas parītyatha mitram upatiṣṭhate pra mitrāya prāryamṇa iti sa yadi sūryābhyuditaḥ sūryābhinimrukto vā taccheṣaṃ sāvitrīṃ manasā dhyāyet saiva tatra prāyaścittiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Evening and morning, having become pure at the water's edge and wearing a pavitra, he should cleanse himself with water with the three verses beginning "The waters are most wholesome," or with the four verses beginning "He crosses, the gladdening one runs," with the Vāmadevya at the end. Sitting on darbha grass in a clean place, holding darbhas, facing west, and restrained in speech, he should meditate mentally on the saṃdhyā until the rising of the stars. When the stars have risen, after holding three breath-controls, he should repeat the Sāvitrī a thousand times, or a hundred times, or at least ten times. Then he attends upon <s>Agni</s> with "Agni, you are nearest to us." Then he attends upon <s>Varuṇa</s> with "You, Varuṇa, and also Mitra." By the same procedure in the morning, standing and facing east, he attends upon <s>Āditya</s> with "We have gone up from darkness," and then upon <s>Mitra</s> with "For Mitra and Aryaman." If he has been overtaken by sunrise or by sunset, he should mentally meditate on the remaining portion of the Sāvitrī; that itself is the expiation there.

children.text: śrāvaṇyām upākaraṇaṃ prauṣṭhapadyāṃ vā hastena trīn prāṇāyāmān āyamyācamya sarve purastājjapaṃ japanti saha no 'stu saha no bhunaktu saha no vīryavad astu mā vidviṣāmahe sarveṣāṃ no vīryavad astviti tebhyaḥ sāvitrīṃ prabrūyād yathopanayane manasā sāmasāvitrīṃ ca somaṃ rājānam ityāditaśchandāṃsyadhītya yathārtham akṣatadhānānāṃ dadhnaśca navāhutīr juhoty ṛṣīn devāṃśchandāṃsy ṛco yajūṃṣi sāmāny ṛcaṃ sāma yajāmahe sadasaspatim adbhutaṃ medhākāram ityetāsām eva pūrvābhiḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ pūrvaṃ tarpayed ācāryam ācāryāṃśca jaiminiṃ talavakāraṃ sātyamugraṃ rāṇāyaniṃ durvāsasaṃ ca bhāguriṃ gauruṇḍiṃ gaurgulaviṃ bhagavantam aupamanyavaṃ kāraḍiṃ sāvarṇiṃ gārgyaṃ vārṣagaṇyaṃ daivantyam ityetāṃstrayodaśa dhānāvantaṃ dadhikrāvṇa ityetābhyām abhimantrya haviḥśeṣaṃ prāśya prāhṇe pradhīyata āgneye samāpte 'ja aindre meṣo gauḥ pāvamāne parvadakṣiṇā sa brahmacāriṇaś copasametān bhojayet sāvitram ahaḥ kāṅkṣanta utsarge ca pakṣiṇīṃ rātriṃ na māṃsam aśnīyānna śrāddhaṃ na lomāni saṃhārayenna striyam upeyād ṛtau jāyām upeyād varṣāśaradikam etadvratam ardhamāsam ityeke ||
children.translated_text: At the Śrāvaṇī, or at the Prauṣṭhapadī under Hasta, the upākaraṇa is performed. Having restrained the breath three times and sipped water, all recite the preliminary muttering: "May it be with us; may it enjoy with us; may there be strength with us; may we not hate one another; may there be strength for us all." He should teach them the Sāvitrī, as at initiation, mentally, and also the Sāma-Sāvitrī. Having studied the metres from the beginning with "Soma the king," he offers, according to the purpose, nine oblations of unhusked rice grains and curds: to the seers, to the gods, to the metres, to the ṛcs, to the yajuses, to the sāmans, to ṛc and sāman, and with "We sacrifice to Sadasaspati, wondrous maker of intelligence." With the first six of these same formulas he should first satisfy the teacher and the teachers: <s>Jaimini</s>, <s>Talavakāra</s>, <s>Sātyamugra</s>, <s>Rāṇāyani</s>, <s>Durvāsas</s>, <s>Bhāguri</s>, <s>Gauruṇḍi</s>, <s>Gaurgulavi</s>, the venerable <s>Aupamanyava</s>, <s>Kāraḍi</s>, <s>Sāvarṇi</s>, <s>Gārgya</s>, <s>Vārṣagaṇya</s>, and <s>Daivantya</s>: these thirteen. After consecrating the grain-filled remainder of the oblation with the two verses beginning "Dadhikrāvan," he eats it. In the forenoon study is begun. When the section belonging to <s>Agni</s> is completed, the dakṣiṇā is a goat; when the section belonging to <s>Indra</s> is completed, a ram; when the Pāvamāna is completed, a cow together with the ceremonial fee at the section's end. He should feed the brahmacārins who have assembled. Expecting the day sacred to the Sāvitrī, and also at the utsarga, for a fortnight of nights he should not eat meat, should not partake of a śrāddha, should not cut his hair, and should not approach a woman; in her season he may approach his wife. This vow lasts through the rainy season and autumn; some say for half a month.

children.text: taiṣīm utsargo vedeṣu yathāsvaṃ viśramantāṃ chandāṃsi caturuttarāṇi śivena no dhyāyantvity utsṛjyādhyāyānadhyāyair vratāni cānupālayanto yathāsvaṃ vedam adhīyīrann ata ūrdhvam abhreṣu nādhīyate ||
children.translated_text: Their utsarga in the Vedas is as follows. Saying, "Let the metres rest each in its own place; let the four-plus metres meditate upon us auspiciously," he releases the studies. Then, observing the vows together with days of study and non-study, they should study their own Veda. From that time onward one does not study when there are clouds.

children.text: gaudānikavrātikaupaniṣadāḥ saṃvatsarāsteṣu sāyaṃprātar udakopasparśanaṃ nānupaspṛśya bhojanaṃ prātaḥ sāyam upaspṛśyā samidādhānād araṇyāt samidham āhṛtyādadhyād ādityavrātikaḥ saṃvatsara ekavāsā na yuktam ārohed ādityaṃ nāntardadhīta chattreṇa mahīm āsanaśayanābhyām upānadbhyāṃ ca nordhvaṃ jānvor apaḥ prasnāyād anyatrācāryavacanād vrātike vrataparvādityavrātike śukriyāṇyaupaniṣada upaniṣadaṃ śrāvayet ||
children.translated_text: The vows called Gaudānika, Vrātika, and Aupaniṣada last for one year. In them, evening and morning, there is touching water; one must not eat without first touching water. Morning and evening, having touched water, he should lay on fuel-sticks: bringing a fuel-stick from the forest, he should place it on the fire. The Āditya-vrātika lasts for one year. He wears a single garment, must not mount a yoked vehicle, must not screen himself from the sun with an umbrella, nor from the earth with a seat, bed, or shoes, and must not bathe in water above the knees, except at the teacher's command. In the Vrātika observance the vow concerns the vow-sections; in the Āditya-vrātika, the Śukriya sections; in the Aupaniṣada, he should teach the Upaniṣad.

children.text: dvādaśa mahānāmnikāḥ saṃvatsarā nava ṣaṭ traya iti vikalpāḥ saṃvatsaram ityeke pitrā cecchrutā mahānāmnyaḥ saṃvatsaraṃ brahmacaryaṃ carecchuklaikavāsā vrataṃ tu bhūyas tiṣṭhed divāthāsīta naktaṃ tasya kṛṣṇe bhojanācchādane bhavata ityeke śuklaṃ caiva paridadhyād rāgadoṣānna kṛṣṇaṃ sarvāsvapsūpaspṛśed abuktāḥ śakvarya iti nāvā na prasnāyāt prāṇasaṃśaye tūpaspṛśed ubhayato 'pi vā gāḥ pāyayet paśūktāḥ śakvarya iti varṣaṃ nāntardadhīta chattreṇa prati varṣaṃ niṣkrāmed evam asya carataḥ kāmavarṣī parjanyo bhavati brahmacaryānta ekarātram upoṣita araṇyaṃ gatvā śaivalamiśrāṇām apāṃ kāṃsaṃ pūrayitvā tam upaveśya samanuparigṛhya nimīlitaṃ tisraḥ stotriyā upagāyet sapurīṣā upotthāyācāryo 'hatena vāsasā mukham asya pariṇahyet pradakṣiṇam udapātraṃ dhārayaṃstiṣṭhed ahaḥśeṣaṃ rātrim āsīta vāgyataḥ śvobhūte 'raṇyaṃ gatvāgnim upasamādhāya vatsam upānvānīya vāsa udveṣṭayed udyamya kāṃsam apo 'bhivīkṣa iti vīkṣet svar abhivīkṣa ityādityaṃ jyotir abhivīkṣa ityagniṃ paśum abhivīkṣa iti vatsaṃ sam anyā yantīty apaḥ prasicya vāsaḥ kāṃsaṃ vatsam ityācāryāyopaharet sthālīpākād viśvāmitrendrau mahānāmnīśca yajata ityācāryaṃ sapariṣaṭkaṃ bhojayed gaur dakṣiṇā ||
children.translated_text: The Mahānāmnī observances last twelve years; alternatives are nine, six, or three years. Some say one year. If the Mahānāmnīs have been heard from his father, he should practice brahmacarya for one year. Wearing a single white garment, he should stand for most of the vow by day and sit at night. Some say that his food and covering during it are black. But he should wear only white; because of the fault of dye he should not wear black. He should touch water in all waters. The Śakvarī verses are said to be "unexperienced"; he should not bathe from a boat. But when life is in danger he may touch water, or he may water cows on both sides, for the Śakvarī verses are said to be "cattle-spoken." For a year he should not screen himself with an umbrella. Each year he should go out toward the rain. When he conducts himself in this way, <s>Parjanya</s> rains according to his desire. At the end of the brahmacarya, having fasted for one night, he goes to the forest, fills a bronze vessel with water mixed with moss, seats him there, embraces him from behind, and, while his eyes are closed, sings three stotriya verses near him, together with their purīṣa verses. Rising up, the teacher wraps his face with an unworn garment and stands for the remainder of the day holding the water-vessel clockwise; or he sits through the night, restrained in speech. On the following day, having gone to the forest, set the fire in place, and led up a calf, he unwraps the garment. Raising the bronze vessel, he says, "Look upon the waters," and he looks; "Look upon the sun," and he looks at the sun; "Look upon the light," and he looks at the fire; "Look upon the animal," and he looks at the calf. With "They go together elsewhere," he pours out the waters. He should present the garment, the bronze vessel, and the calf to the teacher. From a sthālīpāka he sacrifices to <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and the Mahānāmnīs, and he should feed the teacher together with his company. A cow is the dakṣiṇā.

children.text: dvādaśa varṣāṇi vedabrahmacaryaṃ jananāt prabhṛtītyeke yāvadadhyayanaṃ vā sadā sāye samidādhānaṃ sāyaṃprātar bhaikṣacaraṇaṃ dve trivṛtī varjayet trivṛtaṃ ca maṇiṃ triguṇe copānahau ṣoḍaśe godānakaraṇaṃ tat keśāntakaraṇam ityācakṣate cauḍakaraṇena mantrā vyākhyātā upanayanena vratadeśanaṃ na tviha niyuktam ahataṃ vāsaḥ sarvāṇi lomanakhāni vāpayecchikhāvarjam ityaudgāhamanir uptakeśaḥ snāyād vanaspater iti vanaspatīnāṃ snānīyena tvacam unmṛdnīte vanaspatestvag asi śodhani śodhaya mā tāṃ tvābhihare dīrghāyuṣṭvāya varcasa iti vanaspatīnāṃ gandho 'sīti snātvānulepanena kurute vanaspatīnāṃ gandho 'si puṇyagandha puṇyaṃ me gandhaṃ kuru devamanuṣyeṣu taṃ tvābhihare dīrghāyuṣṭvāya varcasa iti vanaspatīnāṃ puṣpam asīti srajam ābadhnīte vanaspatīnāṃ puṣpam asi puṇyagandha puṇyaṃ me gandhaṃ kuru devamanuṣyeṣu taṃ tvābhihare dīrghāyuṣṭvāya varcasa ityādarśo 'sītyādarśa ātmānaṃ vīkṣetādarśo 'sy ā mā dṛśyāsan devamanuṣyā ubhaye śobho 'si śobhāsam ahaṃ devamanuṣyeṣu roco 'si rocāsam ahaṃ devamanuṣyeṣvityapoddhṛtya srajam ādeśayetoktā dharmāḥ saṃvatsareṣu gaur dakṣiṇā ||
children.translated_text: Some say that the Vedic brahmacarya should last twelve years from birth onward, or until the completion of study. Always, in the evening he should place fuel on the fire, and in the evening and morning he should go for alms. He should avoid two threefold things: a threefold jewel and sandals with three layers. In the sixteenth year there is the performance of the godāna; they call that the keśānta rite. The mantras have been explained by the cūḍākaraṇa, and the instruction in the vow by the upanayana; but it is not prescribed here. He should have an unworn garment put on, and should have all his hair and nails cut, except for the topknot. With the formula, 'A shaven-haired man should bathe by means of the forest tree,' he bathes. With the bathing substance of the forest trees he rubs the skin, saying, 'You are the bark of the forest tree, a purifier; purify me. I bring you here for long life and brilliance.' children.translated_text: Having studied the <s>Veda</s> and observed the vows, a brāhmaṇa who is about to take the snātaka bath prepares the requisites: an unworn garment, erakā grass, bathing water, ointment, pleasant flowers, collyrium, a mirror, two unworn garments, a three-stranded jewel, a bamboo staff, and white sandals. A barber, made ready, stands by on the north. Having spread the erakā grass, covered it with the unworn garment with its fringe toward the north, and seated him there facing east, he should set the staff down in the waters, saying, "You are the thunderbolt against enemies." He should loosen the girdle with "Up, highest one," and set that also down in the waters. The mantras for the cutting of the hair-ends, and the shaving, have been explained. He shaves the head first, then the beard, then the other limbs in order. He should bury the hair of the head, beard, body, and nails at the root of an aśvattha tree or of an udumbara, saying, "My sin has been struck away." With cold and warm waters, with gold placed within them, he should bathe him, saying, "Be auspicious for us, most peaceful, very gracious, O <s>Sarasvatī</s>; do not make your expanse visible." He should bathe under <s>Rohiṇī</s>, thinking, "This is <s>Prajāpati</s>'s asterism; may I be rich in offspring." He should bathe under <s>Mṛgaśiras</s>, thinking, "This is <s>Soma</s>'s asterism; may the soma-sacrifice come near to me." He should bathe under <s>Tiṣya</s>, thinking, "This is <s>Bṛhaspati</s>'s asterism; <s>Bṛhaspati</s> is brahman; may I possess brahmanic splendor." He should bathe under <s>Hasta</s>, thinking, "This is <s>Savitṛ</s>'s asterism; may I be impelled by <s>Savitṛ</s>." He should bathe under the <s>Anūrādhās</s>, thinking, "This is <s>Mitra</s>'s asterism; may I be dear to friends." He should bathe under <s>Śravaṇa</s>, thinking, "This is <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s asterism; sacrifice indeed is <s>Viṣṇu</s>; may sacrifice come near to me." He should clothe him with the unworn garment, saying, "Around this one, O <s>Soma</s>." He first anoints the left eye, saying, "With glory," and then the right. He fastens the three-stranded jewel on his neck: one of palāśa wood if he desires well-being, saying, "You are a bringer of well-being"; one of bilva if he desires brahmanic splendor, saying, "May I possess brahmanic splendor"; one of arka if he desires food to eat, saying, "May I possess arka and be an eater of food." Saying, "You are the gandharva <s>Viśvāvasu</s>; protect me, guard me," he takes up the bamboo staff. He should put on the sandals, saying, "You are two eyes; lead me," fastening the right one first. His vows are these: he should not seek mockery from one whose body-hair has not yet appeared; he should not run when it rains; he should not carry his sandals himself; he should not gather fruits himself; he should not go to another village every evening; he should not be alone with vṛṣalas; he should not look into a well; he should not climb a tree; he should not climb onto a crossing; he should not sit without an intervening screen; he should not eat food brought in by a lower door; he should not eat sour food, twice-cooked food, or stale food, except vegetables, meat, barley flour, rice cakes, parched grain, molasses, curds, honey, and ghee; he should not laugh except in jest; he should not bathe naked; he should not speak corrupt words; and he should avoid gossip and quarrels. There are three kinds of snātakas, so <s>Āruṇi Gautama</s> used to say: one bathed after learning, one bathed after vows, and one bathed after both learning and vows. Of these the last is best; the first two are equal. After bathing he should say to the teacher, "Let my lord bring me a madhuparka," or one who is equivalent to the teacher should bring the madhuparka for him as he sits facing east. The seat, foot-water, arghya, and sipping-water are brought one after another. He sits on the seat and washes his feet with the foot-water, first the left foot, saying, "May prosperity rest in me"; if the washer is a śūdra, "May royal splendor enter me through the feet"; then the right foot, saying, "May brilliance be in me." He should receive the arghya and sip with the sipping-waters. The vessel or cup is placed upon a seat; beneath it are two seats with their tips joined, or one seat to the north. In their midst curds and honey are set together. If it is made with curds, it is curd-mixture; if with water, water-mixture; if with milk, milk-mixture. He should receive it with "Of the god, you," and having received it, set it on the ground, rub it with the thumb and the finger next to the little finger, and taste it three times, saying, "You are for my glory, food, and brahmanic splendor." Taking the remainder to the north, he should give it to a brāhmaṇa; or, after sprinkling it, to a non-brāhmaṇa; or he should bury it in a pit. Another man, holding an axe in his hand, on seeing the cow says, "A cow, a cow." He addresses her with the mantra, "The cow is a milch cow," and should say, "Om, release her." If she is to be slaughtered, he should say, "Do it." children.translated_text: "May my husband be long-lived; may my kinsmen prosper. Svāhā."

children.text: aryamṇaṃ nu devaṃ kanyāgnim ayakṣata
children.translated_text: The maiden has now sacrificed to the god <s>Aryaman</s> and to <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: sa imāṃ devo aryamā preto muñcātu māmutaḥ svāheti
children.translated_text: May the god <s>Aryaman</s>, when he has gone forth, release this woman from here and not me. Svāhā.

children.translated_text: At the ends of the oblations he mutters, "O you four, all of you, and with you may we, like streams full of water,

children.text: atigāhemahi dviṣa iti tūṣṇīṃ dhārikā kāmāyāvapeccaturthaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ śūrpapuṭaṃ kāma ityācakṣata uttarapurastād agneḥ sapta padānyabhyutkramayed ekam iṣa iti pratimantram ekam iṣe viṣṇustvānvetu
children.translated_text: pass beyond hostility." Silently the girl should pour a fourth portion for desire. The southern corner of the winnowing basket is called "desire." To the north-east of the fire he should make her take seven steps, one at each mantra: "One for nourishment: may <s>Viṣṇu</s> follow you.

children.text: trīṇi rāyaspoṣāya viṣṇustvānvetu
children.translated_text: Three for increase of wealth: may <s>Viṣṇu</s> follow you.
