children.text: pañca prajābhyo viṣṇustvānvetu
children.translated_text: Five for offspring: may <s>Viṣṇu</s> follow you.

children.text: ṣaḍ ṛtubhyo viṣṇustvānvetu
children.translated_text: Six for the seasons: may <s>Viṣṇu</s> follow you.

children.text: sakhā saptapadī bhaveti saptame prācīm avasthāpyodakumbhena mārjayerann āpohiṣṭhīyābhistisṛbhiḥ prekṣakān anumantrayate sumaṅgalīr iyaṃ vadhūr imāṃ sameta paśyata
children.translated_text: Be my friend, one who has taken the seven steps." At the seventh step, having set her facing east, they should sprinkle her with a water-pot with the three verses beginning "The waters are most wholesome." He addresses the onlookers: "This bride is auspicious; assemble and look upon her.

children.text: saubhāgyam asyai dattvāyāthāstaṃ viparetaneti prekṣayed dhruvam arundhatīṃ sapta ṛṣīn paśyānīti pratijānānāṃ dhruvo 'sīti dhruvam upatiṣṭhate dhruvo 'si dhruvāhaṃ patikule bhūyāsam amuṣyeti patināma gṛhṇīyād asāvityātmano 'rundhatīm arundhatyaruddhāhaṃ patyā bhūyāsam amuneti patināma gṛhṇīyād asāvityātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having given her good fortune, go each back to your own house." He should make her look at <s>Dhruva</s>, <s>Arundhatī</s>, and the Seven Seers. When she promises, "I see," he attends upon <s>Dhruva</s>: "You are firm; may I be firm in my husband's family, belonging to so-and-so," naming the husband; "so-and-so," naming herself. Then he attends upon <s>Arundhatī</s>: "O <s>Arundhatī</s>, may I be unopposed by my husband, by so-and-so," naming the husband; "so-and-so," naming herself.

children.text: pūṣā tveta iti prasthitām anumantryate pūṣā tveto nayatu hastagṛhyāśvinau tvā pravahatāṃ rathena
children.translated_text: As she sets out, he addresses her with "<s>Pūṣan</s> has led you": "May <s>Pūṣan</s> lead you from here, taking you by the hand; may the two <s>Aśvins</s> carry you forward by chariot.

children.text: gṛhān gaccha gṛhapatnī yathāso vaśinī tvaṃ vidatham āvadāsīti svaṃ kulaṃ prāptāṃ kalyāṇaśīlāḥ kalyāṇaprajāḥ samavajīrṇāḥ pratyavaropayantīha priyaṃ prajayā te samṛdhyatām asmin gṛhe gārhapatyāya jāgṛhi
children.translated_text: Go to the house, so that you may be mistress of the house; you, commanding, shall speak in the assembly." When she has reached his own family, women of good character, with good offspring and grown old with their husbands, make her descend: "Here may what is dear to you prosper with offspring; in this house keep watch over the gārhapatya fire.

children.text: enā patyā tanvaṃ saṃsṛjasvāthājīvro vidatham āvadāsīti pratyavaropyānaḍuhe carmaṇyuttaralomanyupaveśayed iha gāvo niṣīdantvihāśvā iha puruṣāḥ
children.translated_text: With this husband join your body; then, full of life, you shall speak in the assembly." Having made her descend, he should seat her on the hide of a bull, with the hair turned upward: "Here may cows sit down; here may horses; here may men.

children.text: iho sahasradakṣiṇo 'bhi pūṣā niṣīdatviti kumāram upastha ādhāya śakaloṭān āvapet phalāni votthāpya kumāram anvārabdhāyāṃ juhuyād iha dhṛtir ityaṣṭābhiḥ svāhākārān tair iha dhṛtir iha svadhṛtir iha rantir iha ramasva
children.translated_text: Here may <s>Pūṣan</s>, rich in a thousand gifts, sit down." Placing a boy in her lap, he should pour pieces of śakala, or fruits. Having raised the boy, while she touches him from behind, he should offer with the eight formulas beginning "Here is steadfastness," with svāhā-calls: "Here is steadfastness; here is firm steadfastness; here is delight; here delight yourself.

children.text: mayi dhṛtir mayi svadhṛtir mayi ramo mayi ramasveti trirātram akṣārālavaṇāśinau brahmacāriṇāvadhaḥ saṃveśināvasaṃvartamānau saha śayātām ūrdhvaṃ trirātrāt saṃbhavo niśāyāṃ jāyāpatikarmaṇyaṃ prāyaścittīr juhuyād agne prāyaścitte tvaṃ devānāṃ prāyaścittir asi brāhmaṇastvā nāthakāma upadhāvāmi yāsyai prajāghnī tanūstām asyā upajahi svāhā
children.translated_text: In me is steadfastness; in me is firm steadfastness; in me is pleasure; in me delight yourself." For three nights the two should eat food without alkali and without salt, live as brahmacārins, sleep below, avoid turning toward one another, and sleep together. After three nights, union takes place at night. In the rite of husband and wife he should offer expiatory oblations: "O <s>Agni</s>, in expiation you are the expiation of the gods. As a brāhmaṇa desiring protection, I approach you. Whatever body of hers destroys offspring, strike that away from her. Svāhā.

children.text: vāyo prāyaścitte tvaṃ devānāṃ prāyaścittir asi brāhmaṇastvā nāthakāma upadhāvāmi yāsyai paśughnī tanūstām asyā upajahi svāhā
children.translated_text: O <s>Vāyu</s>, in expiation you are the expiation of the gods. As a brāhmaṇa desiring protection, I approach you. Whatever body of hers destroys cattle, strike that away from her. Svāhā.

children.text: sūrya prāyaścitte tvaṃ devānāṃ prāyaścittir asi brāhmaṇastvā nāthakāma upadhāvāmi yāsyai patighnī tanūstām asyā upajahi svāhā
children.translated_text: O <s>Sūrya</s>, in expiation you are the expiation of the gods. As a brāhmaṇa desiring protection, I approach you. Whatever body of hers destroys the husband, strike that away from her. Svāhā.

children.text: candra prāyaścitte tvaṃ devānāṃ prāyaścittir asi brāhmaṇastvā nāthakāma upadhāvāmi yāsyai gṛhaghnī tanūstām asyā upajahi svāhā
children.translated_text: O <s>Candra</s>, in expiation you are the expiation of the gods. As a brāhmaṇa desiring protection, I approach you. Whatever body of hers destroys the household, strike that away from her. Svāhā.

children.text: agne vāyo sūrya candra prāyaścittayo yūyaṃ devānāṃ prāyaścittayaḥ stha brāhmaṇo vo nāthakāma upadhāvāmi yāsyai yaśoghnī tanūstām asyā upahata svāheti sthālīpākād agniṃ prajāpatiṃ ceṣṭvā saṃpātāṃścamasa ānīya srotāṃsyāṅkṣvetyenāṃ brūyānnābhiṃ prathamaṃ tato yāny ūrdhvaṃ tato yānyarvāñcy ūrdhvam ardharātrāt saṃveśanaṃ viṣṇur yoniṃ kalpayatvityetena tṛcena viṣṇur yoniṃ kalpayatu tvaṣṭā rūpāṇi piṃśatu
children.translated_text: O <s>Agni</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Sūrya</s>, and <s>Candra</s>, you are expiations, the expiations of the gods. As a brāhmaṇa desiring protection, I approach you. Whatever body of hers destroys fame, strike that away from her. Svāhā." Then, having sacrificed to <s>Agni</s> and <s>Prajāpati</s> from a sthālīpāka and brought the saṃpātas into a cup, he should say to her, "Anoint the channels," first the navel, then those above, then those below. After midnight is the lying together, with this triad beginning "May <s>Viṣṇu</s> prepare the womb": "May <s>Viṣṇu</s> prepare the womb; may <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> fashion the forms.

children.text: āsiñcatu prajāpatir dhātā garbhaṃ dadhātu te
children.translated_text: May <s>Prajāpati</s> pour in; may <s>Dhātṛ</s> place the embryo in you.

children.text: garbhaṃ dhehi sinīvāli garbhaṃ dhehi sarasvati
children.translated_text: Place the embryo, O <s>Sinīvālī</s>; place the embryo, O <s>Sarasvatī</s>.

children.text: garbhaṃ te aśvinau devāvādhattāṃ puṣkarasrajau
children.translated_text: May the two divine <s>Aśvins</s>, garlanded with lotuses, set the embryo in you."

children.text: hiraṇyayī araṇī yaṃ nirmanthatām aśvinau
children.translated_text: "The golden araṇī, which the two <s>Aśvins</s> should churn forth,"

children.text: taṃ te garbhaṃ dadhāmyahaṃ daśame māsi sūtavā ityṛtāvṛtāvevam eva saṃveśane hutvācāryāya gāṃ dadyād adarśane brāhmaṇebhyo gāṃ dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: "that embryo of yours I place; in the tenth month may she give birth." Thus, in each season, after offering in this way at cohabitation, he should give a cow to the teacher; if the teacher is not present, he should give a cow to brāhmaṇas.

children.text: sāyaṃprātarhome 'gnaya iti prathamām āhutiṃ juhoti prajāpataya ityuttarām evaṃ prātar agnisthāne sūryaḥ sāyaṃprātaraśanasya balī vardhayitvā pūrvasmād agnau juhotyagnaye svāhā somāya svāhā dhanvantaraye svāhā dyāvāpṛthivībhyāṃ svāhā viśvebhyo devebhyaḥ svāhā sarvābhyo devatābhyaḥ svāhā prajāpataye svāheti manasottarāṃ tata evottarato 'gner baliṃ harati ye harṣaṇā vepanā sphātim āharā vātasya bhrājam anusaṃcaranti
children.translated_text: At the evening and morning homa he offers the first oblation with "to the <s>Agnis</s>," and the second with "to <s>Prajāpati</s>." In the same way, in the morning the sun is in place of the fire. Having increased the bali of the evening and morning meal, he offers in the fire from the eastern portion: "to <s>Agni</s>, svāhā; to <s>Soma</s>, svāhā; to <s>Dhanvantari</s>, svāhā; to Heaven and Earth, svāhā; to all the gods, svāhā; to all the deities, svāhā; to <s>Prajāpati</s>, svāhā." The last he offers mentally. From there, to the north of the fire, he carries the bali: "Those who are gladdeners, tremblers, bringers of swelling increase, who move along after the shining of the wind,

children.text: tebhyo balim annakāmo harāmyannaṃ payasvad bahulaṃ me astvityevam aśanāyatyāyasthāne mṛtyor adhiṣṭhānāya svāheti śeṣasya baliharaṇaṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ gṛhyābhyo devatābhyo baliṃ nayāmi tanme juṣantāṃ tā mā pāntu tā mā gopāyantu tā mā rakṣantu tābhyo namastābhyaḥ svāhetyudadhāne madhye 'gārasyottarapūrvārdhe śayane dehalyāṃ saṃvaraṇe brahmāyatana eteṣvāyataneṣu śeṣaṃ dhanvantaraye ninayet sadā gṛheṣu svastivācanaṃ sā mahāśāntir ityācakṣate ||
children.translated_text: to them, desiring food, I carry bali. May food rich in milk and abundant be mine." Thus when he is hungry. At the place assigned to trouble he offers, "svāhā to the seat of Death." The carrying of the remaining bali is clockwise: "I lead the bali to the domestic deities. May they accept that from me; may they protect me; may they guard me; may they preserve me. Homage to them, svāhā to them." At the water-jar, in the middle of the house, in the north-eastern part, on the bed, on the threshold, at the covering, and at the place of brahman: at these places he should pour out the remainder for <s>Dhanvantari</s>. Constantly in the houses there is a recitation for well-being; they call that the Great Pacification.

children.text: navena yakṣyamāṇaḥ purāṇenāgre yajetāgnidhanvantarī prajāpatim indraṃ tisraśca navāhutīr navena yajeta śaradi vrīhīṇāṃ vasante yavānāṃ varṣāsu śyāmākānām aindrāgno vaiśvadevo dyāvāpṛthivyaścarava ekacarur vokte evopastaraṇābhighāraṇe dvir haviṣo 'vadyatyatha prāśnīyād bhadrānnaḥ śreyaḥ samanaiṣṭa devāstvayāvasena samaśīmahi tvā
children.translated_text: When he is about to sacrifice with new grain, he should first sacrifice with old grain. With the new grain he should sacrifice to <s>Agni</s>, <s>Dhanvantari</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s>, and <s>Indra</s>, and make three new-grain oblations. He should sacrifice with rice in autumn, with barley in spring, and with śyāmāka millet in the rains. The carus belong to <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>, to all the gods, and to Heaven and Earth; or else one single caru is prescribed. The placing underneath and the sprinkling over are just as stated. He cuts off from the oblation twice, and then he should taste it: "May the gods together bring us good and prosperity; through your favor may we partake of you.

children.text: sa no mayobhūḥ pito āviśasva śaṃ tokāya tanuve syona ityetam u tyaṃ madhunā saṃyutaṃ yavaṃ sarasvatyā adhi manāvacarkṛṣuḥ
children.translated_text: Be for us a source of delight, O food; enter us, auspicious for offspring and body." "This barley, joined with honey, they have stirred upon the mind of <s>Sarasvatī</s>.

children.text: indra āsīt sīrapatiḥ śatakratuḥ kīnāśā āsanmarutaḥ sudānava iti yavasya prāśnīyād agniḥ prathamaḥ prāśnātu sa hi veda yathā haviḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s>, of a hundred powers, was lord of the plough; the ploughmen were the generous <s>Maruts</s>." Thus he should taste the barley. "Let <s>Agni</s> taste first, for he knows how the oblation is."

children.text: śivā asmabhyam oṣadhīḥ kṛṇotu viśvacarṣaṇīr iti śyāmākasya prāśnīyāt ||
children.translated_text: "May the plants, active among all peoples, make things auspicious for us." Thus he should taste the śyāmāka millet.

children.text: Chapter 2

śrāddhaṃ kariṣyantaḥ snātāḥ śucivāsasas tilair vāstvavakīrya savyam ācaranto 'nnam upasādhayeran haviṣyair upasicyaivaivaṃ dadyād yad yad dadyāt tattaddhaviṣyair upasicyaiva haviṣyā iti tilānām ākhyā dantadhāvanaṃ snānīyāni pādyam ānīya prathamoddhṛtaṃ brāhmaṇāṃstryavadātān upaveśayatyā me gacchantu pitaro bhāgadheyaṃ virājāhūtāḥ salilāt samudriyāt ||
children.translated_text: Those who are about to perform a śrāddha, having bathed and wearing clean garments, should scatter sesame seeds over the dwelling-place, proceed keeping the left side foremost, and prepare the food. Having sprinkled it with sacrificial foods, he should give it in just this way: whatever he gives, he should sprinkle each thing with sacrificial foods. "Sacrificial foods" is the designation of the sesame seeds. Having brought tooth-cleaning sticks, bathing materials, and foot-water, he seats the brāhmaṇas, who are purified in three ways, on the first seats laid out: "May the fathers come to me, to their allotted share, invoked by <s>Virāj</s>, from the waters, from the ocean.

children.text: akṣīyamāṇam upajīvatainan mayā prattaṃ svadhayā madadhvam ityupamūlalūnān darbhān viṣṭarān prasavyān kṛtvā brāhmaṇebhyaḥ pradadyād etat te pitar āsanam asau ye ca tvātrānu tebhyaścāsanam ityevaṃ pitāmahāyaivaṃ prapitāmahāya haviṣyodakaṃ tiraḥ pavitraṃ gandhān sumanasaś ca dadyād annam avattvā ghṛtenābhighārya darbhān paristaraṇīyān iti tad ādāyāgnau kariṣyāmīti brāhmaṇān anujñāpya prāgdakṣiṇāmukho 'gniṃ praṇayitvā trir dhūnvan pradakṣiṇam agniṃ paristṛṇāti prācīnāvītī triḥ prasavyaṃ triḥ paryukṣet pradakṣiṇaṃ prācīnāvītī triḥ prasavyam audumbara idhmaḥ paridhayo bhavanti mekṣaṇaṃ ca pavitraṃ saṃskṛtyānnam utpūyāgnau pavitraṃ prāsya mekṣaṇena juhotyagnaye kavyavāhanāya svadhā namaḥ svāhā somāya pitṛmate svadhā namaḥ svāheti yajñopavītī bhūtvāpa upaspṛśya yamāyā ||
children.translated_text: "Live upon this inexhaustible thing given by me; rejoice with svadhā." Having made seats of darbha grass cut near the root, with their tips turned counterclockwise, he should give them to the brāhmaṇas: "This is your seat, father so-and-so, and also for those who follow you here; for them too this is a seat." In the same way for the grandfather and in the same way for the great-grandfather. He should give water for the oblation through the strainer, and fragrances and flowers. Having cut off food, sprinkled it with ghee, and taken up the darbhas for strewing, he asks the brāhmaṇas' permission, saying, "I shall perform it in the fire." Facing east-south, he sets the fire in motion and, shaking three times, strews around the fire clockwise. Wearing the sacred thread over the right shoulder, he should sprinkle three times counterclockwise, then clockwise; wearing the thread over the right shoulder, three times counterclockwise. The fuel and enclosing sticks are of udumbara wood. Having prepared the mekṣaṇa ladle and the strainer, strained the food, and thrown the strainer into the fire, he offers with the mekṣaṇa: "to <s>Agni</s>, carrier of the kavya, svadhā, homage, svāhā; to <s>Soma</s>, accompanied by the fathers, svadhā, homage, svāhā." Having put on the yajñopavīta and touched water, to <s>Yama</s>:

children.text: akṣīyamāṇām upajīvatainan mayā prattaṃ svadhayā madadhvam ||
children.translated_text: "Live upon this inexhaustible thing given by me; rejoice with svadhā."

children.text: amṛtā vāg amṛtā vāco agne vāco 'mṛtatvaṃ trivṛtaikadhāmā ||
children.translated_text: "Speech is immortal; the words are immortal. O <s>Agni</s> of speech, the immortality of speech is in the threefold single abode."

children.text: ebhir mat prattaiḥ svadhayā madadhvam ihāsmabhyaṃ vasīyo 'stu devāḥ ||
children.translated_text: "With these things given by me, rejoice with svadhā. May there be something better for us here, O gods."

children.text: ayaṃ yajñaḥ paramo yaḥ pitṝṇāṃ pātradeyaṃ pitṛdaivatyam agne ||
children.translated_text: "This sacrifice, which belongs to the fathers, is supreme; O <s>Agni</s>, the gift to the vessel is dedicated to the fathers."

children.text: vāk ca manaś ca pitaro naḥ prajānīmāśvibhyāṃ prattaṃ svadhayā madadhvam ||
children.translated_text: "Speech and mind, O fathers, are known to us. What has been given by the two <s>Aśvins</s>, rejoice in it with svadhā."

children.text: ya iha pitaraḥ pārthivāso ye antarikṣa uta ye samudriyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Those fathers here who are earthly, and those who are in the midspace, and those who are oceanic,

children.text: ye vācam āptvā amṛtā babhūvus te 'smin sarve haviṣi mādayantām ||
children.translated_text: those who, having attained speech, have become immortal: may all of them delight in this oblation."

children.text: eṣā va ūrg eṣā vaḥ svadhā cām atta ca pibata ca mā ca vaḥ kṣeṣṭa ||
children.translated_text: "This is your nourishment; this is also your svadhā. Eat and drink, and may it not be exhausted for you."

children.text: svadhāṃ vahadhvam amṛtasya yoniṃ yātra svadhā pitaras tāṃ bhajadhvam ||
children.translated_text: "Carry the svadhā to the womb of immortality; wherever that svadhā is, O fathers, share in it."

children.text: yeha pitara ūrg devatā ca tasyai jīvema śaradaḥ śataṃ vayam ||
children.translated_text: "May we live a hundred autumns for her, for whom the fathers here are nourishment and deity."

children.text: jyotiṣmad dhattājaraṃ ma āyur ityathaitāni brāhmaṇebhya upanikṣipya svā ||
children.translated_text: "Set down the radiant one; let my life be free from old age." Then, having placed these things before the brāhmaṇas, he recites, "Svā."

children.text: ya skandati nirṛtiṃ vāta ugrāṃ yena naḥ prīyante pitaro devatāś ca ||
children.translated_text: "Whatever has fallen, or the fierce <s>Nirṛti</s> and the wind, by which our fathers and the deities are not pleased,

children.text: vāyuṣ ṭat sarvaṃ śundhatu tena śuddhena devatā mādayantāṃ tasmiñchuddhe pitaro mādayantām ityakrān samudra ity āśvaṃ gītvā sampannaṃ pṛṣṭvāthācāmayed yajñopavītī bhūtvābhiramantāṃ bhavanta ity uktvā pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtvā yan me rāmeti gacchato 'numantrayate yan me rāmā śakuniḥ śvāpadaś ca yan me 'śucir mantrakṛtasya prāśat ||
children.translated_text: may <s>Vāyu</s> purify all that. With that purified thing may the deities be gladdened; in that purified thing may the fathers be gladdened." Thus, after reciting "He stepped over the ocean" and singing the āśva chant, after asking whether it has been completed, he should then make him sip water. Having put on the yajñopavīta, saying, "May you gentlemen be pleased," and having gone around clockwise, as he goes he murmurs over it with "What of mine, O Rāmā": "What of mine a woman, a bird, a wild animal, or an impure person has eaten of what was made with mantra,

children.translated_text: Having asked permission for the remainder, he returns, smears with cow-dung a square place stretching east and south, and in the middle draws a line with a piece of wood, saying, "The asuras, rakṣases, and piśācas who sit among the fathers have been driven away." With "Those asuras who assume forms and move about with svadhā, those who bear away, who steal away: may <s>Agni</s> drive them away from this world of ours," he sets down a firebrand on the south. Along the line he spreads darbha grass and, with a vessel of water, makes them sip: "Sip, father so-and-so; and those who follow you here, let them also sip." In the same way for the grandfather and in the same way for the great-grandfather. On those grasses he places the piṇḍas, using the hand with the thumb turned downward and naming each: "This is for you, father so-and-so; and for those who follow you here, svadhā and homage to them." In the same way for the grandfather and in the same way for the great-grandfather. If he does not know the names, he says, "Father, this is for you; grandfather, this is for you; great-grandfather, this is for you." If he does not know the relatives, he says, "This is for the fathers who dwell on earth; this is for the grandfathers who dwell in the midspace; this is for the great-grandfathers who dwell in heaven." Then, "Fathers, be gladdened here; each according to his share, take vigor." Turning northward, he and the other sit silently. After muttering, "The fathers were gladdened; each according to his share they took vigor," he makes them sip as before, lets the sacred thread hang low, makes obeisances, and according to the deity assigns the garments with "This is for you, O fathers": a tuft of wool or a ten-threaded cloth. "This, O fathers, is your garment. Give us homes, O fathers. Bestow, O fathers, an embryo, a boy with a lotus garland, so that a man may be here." He gives collyrium and anointing, saying, "Anoint yourself, so-and-so; smear yourself, so-and-so." He should give fragrances and flowers. With the six obeisances beginning "Homage to you, O fathers," he attends upon them: "Homage to you, O fathers, for sap; homage to you, O fathers, for strength; homage to you, O fathers, for life; homage to you, O fathers, for terror; homage to you, O fathers, for power; homage to you, O fathers, for wrath. To svadhā, and to you, O fathers, homage." Pouring out waters with "Waters bearing nourishment, immortality, ghee, milk, and the fermented sweet drink, you are svadhā; satisfy my fathers," he consecrates them with "Do not be exhausted for me": "Do not be exhausted for me; may what has been filled for me be abundant. May the brāhmaṇas enjoy my food, food.

Of these oblations he should offer in the fire according to the procedure for a sthālīpāka: "To Aṣṭakā, svāhā; to Ekāṣṭakā, svāhā; to Aṣṭakā rich in heroes, svāhā. From her he cuts off three left-side portions: the flank, the loin-cut, and the haunch. On the following day there is the anvaṣṭakya śrāddha, or on that same day. Having seated brāhmaṇas fit for the oblation, and having satisfied them, he should carry six fires south of that fire and have one trench dug at each of them, a span long, three finger-breadths in earth, and one finger-breadth sloping downward. children.translated_text: When the body of an āhitāgni has perished, one should bring three hundred and sixty palāśa leaves with stalks and make an effigy with them on a black antelope skin. He should place eighty and a half on the head, ten on the neck, one hundred on the two arms, again ten on the fingers, thirty on the chest, twenty on the belly, one hundred on the thighs, ten on the penis, thirty on the knees and shanks, and ten also on the toes. Thus it is known that these are the bodily parts of a man. In the middle is the body, the body with the wife, with the hair plucked out and the nails cut, washed; they set it on the pyre. Here he also piles the vessels, and on that he places him. He should put the two sruvas in his nostrils with this anuvāka. A man who knows thus, when he is afflicted, should first take a fourfold ladling; taking another as possible, placing a small piece of gold in the mouth, and carrying up the fires, he attends upon them with sāmans. When the smoke has risen, the village song beginning "The fair-winged one in heaven" is sung. When the smoke has arisen, he says, "Your smoke, flaming, has roared." When the fire has mounted, he uses one of the two verses, "O <s>Agni</s>, be gracious" or "You are great," turning away, for that world is turned away: so says the brāhmaṇa.

children.translated_text: Where plants grow, there, after burning the body, they go to perform the water rite, without looking back. They do not perform it in flowing waters. Whichever among them was born later should perform it first. Near the bank, or where there is no bank after digging a pit, he pours water once with the ring finger of the left hand, naming the deceased. If it is in flowing waters, after loosening their hair and immersing themselves, they give one handful of water, gather up the hair, and then he should touch the fire of the firebrand, saying, "O <s>Agni</s>, burner, strike away my sin." He should touch a śamī tree, saying, "You are śamī; quiet my sin." He should touch a stone, saying, "You are a stone; you are firm; may I become firm." Silently he touches cow-dung and water prepared for the rite. Sitting facing south, the followers sit down around him. The other man addresses them with auspicious words. At the time of sunset they enter the village. That night they live on one māṣa, or on a pacificatory observance. On the following day he mixes milk and water and sprinkles the bones with it, using a goat horn, a cow horn, or an earthen vessel. On the third day, having mixed fragrant herbs, he should cool them with a branch of śamī or palāśa and put them into a jar. If the deceased is a woman, he should put them in a pot. Having passed beyond a crossroads, he should bury them at a great tree, a river, or at sacred bathing places. On the third day they bathe for the deceased with apāmārga, clay, and cow-dung, wash their garments, and sit for ten nights. On the fourth day they should resume begging.

children.translated_text: Now, then, we shall explain the procedure for the fasting recitation of the saṃhitā. He should wear clean garments, or garments of bark. He should wish for sacrificial food as his food, or water, or fruits; but a brāhmaṇa alone should bring it back. Going out from the village toward the east or north, in a clean place or near water, he should smear with cow-dung a raised altar the size of a cowhide, sprinkle it, draw the marks, besprinkle it with water, set the fire down nearby, offer the two āghāras and the two portions of ghee, and offer ghee-oblation to <s>Agni</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s>, <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, all the gods, the seers, the Ṛks, the Yajuses, the Sāmans, Faith, Insight, Intelligence, Sāvitrī, <s>Sadasaspati</s>, and <s>Anumati</s>. Having offered, seated on darbha grass with the tips turned east or north, holding darbhas in his right hand, he should repeat four times the vyāhṛtis preceded by oṃ and the Sāvitrī, and also, mentally, the Sāma-Sāvitrī, "<s>Soma</s> the king," and both "Brahman was born" verses, and then begin from the start of the Veda. He should study continuously, keeping silence, and should not stop in the middle. If he speaks in the middle, or stops in the middle, he should restrain three breaths, sip water, and begin again from the point where the event occurred. In the case of failure of memory, for as much time as he would study the Veda, for that much time he should study. Whatever he knows from the Ṛk, Yajus, or Sāman, he obtains that: its brāhmaṇa, its meter, its deity, or the sāman. Or he may repeat just the formula "The sāman has stepped forth." Standing, sitting, lying down, or walking about, he should apply himself to the saṃhitā; prosperity indeed becomes his. The first trivarga, or a thousand times, so says <s>Jaimini</s>; or up to the Vāryamanta, or according to his desire. Having studied twelve saṃhitās, by them he purifies whatever he has studied on days forbidden for study, whenever teachers have been angered, and whatever improper acts have been done. His brahman becomes pure and purified. Then, having studied another twelve saṃhitās, by them he attains the world of <s>Prajāpati</s>. Then, having studied another twelve saṃhitās, by them he attains the world of <s>Uśanas</s>. Having studied a thousand fasting saṃhitās, he becomes brahman-like and free from stain; moving at will, he obtains all desires. Practicing for a year while living on alms, he obtains sight; for six months living on barley-gruel, for four months living on water and barley-meal, for two months living on fruit, for one month living on water, or for twelve nights fasting, he quickly becomes invisible. He purifies seven ancestors, seven descendants, and himself as the fifteenth; he carries them across. They call this the divine ladder. By this indeed the gods attained godhood and the seers seerhood. This brahma-session has three beginnings only: at the morning pressing, at the midday pressing, or in the brāhma part of the latter night. It has only two occasions forbidden for study: when the self is impure and when the place is impure. <s>Prajāpati</s> taught this to the Seven Seers; the Seven Seers taught it to <s>Mahājahnu</s>; <s>Mahājahnu</s> taught it to the brāhmaṇas.

children.text: Chapter 10
atha grahāṇām ātithyaṃ balikarmoparutaṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ aśraddadhānam aśucikaraṇam ajāpyaṃ tyaktamaṅgalaṃ
children.translated_text: Now we shall explain the hospitality to the planets, the bali rite for averting obstruction: a man who is faithless, who performs impure acts, who does not mutter prayers, and who has abandoned auspicious observances,

children.text: suvyaktaṃ grahā nayanti puruṣaṃ yamasādanam
children.translated_text: the planets very clearly lead him to the abode of <s>Yama</s>.

children.text: grahāṇāṃ dīpraceṣṭānāṃ nakṣatrapathacāriṇām
children.translated_text: For the planets, whose movements are blazing, who travel on the path of the lunar mansions,

children.text: grahātithyaṃ pravakṣyāmi śāntikarmaṇi kārayet
children.translated_text: I shall declare the hospitality to the planets; one should have it performed in a pacificatory rite.

children.text: bhāskarāṅgārakau raktau śvetau śukraniśākarau
children.translated_text: <s>Bhāskara</s> and <s>Aṅgāraka</s> are red; <s>Śukra</s> and the Night-maker are white.

children.text: somaputro guruś caiva tāv ubhau pītakau smṛtau
children.translated_text: The son of <s>Soma</s> and the Guru: those two are remembered as yellow.

children.text: kṛṣṇaṃ śanaiścaraṃ vidyād rāhuṃ ketuṃ tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: One should know <s>Śanaiścara</s> as black, and likewise <s>Rāhu</s> and <s>Ketu</s>.

children.text: grahavarṇāni puṣpāṇi prājñas tatropakalpayet
children.translated_text: A wise man should arrange there flowers having the colors of the planets.

children.text: gomayena gocarmamātraṃ sthaṇḍilam upalipya prokṣya lakṣaṇam ullikhyādbhir abhyukṣyāgnim upasamādhāyāghārāv ājyabhāgau hutvā grahān āvāhayanty ādityaṃ madhye lohitaṃ pūrvadakṣiṇataḥ somam
children.translated_text: Having smeared with cow-dung a raised altar the size of a cowhide, sprinkled it, drawn the marks, besprinkled it with water, set the fire down nearby, and offered the two āghāras and the two portions of ghee, they invoke the planets: <s>Āditya</s> in the middle, red <s>Soma</s> to the southeast,

children.text: pūrvottarato budham uttareṇa guruṃ pūrveṇa bhārgavam
children.translated_text: <s>Budha</s> to the northeast, Guru to the north, and the descendant of <s>Bhṛgu</s> to the east.

children.text: paścime śanaiścaraṃ vidyād rāhuṃ dakṣiṇapaścime paścimottarataḥ ketuṃ vṛttam ādityāya trikoṇam aṅgārakasya caturaśraṃ somāya bāṇaṃ budhāya dīrghacaturaśraṃ bṛhaspataye pañcakoṇaṃ śukrāya dhanuḥ śanaiścarāya rāhoḥ śūrpaṃ ketor dhvajam iti īśvaraṃ bhāskaraṃ vidyāta umāṃ somaṃ tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: One should know <s>Śanaiścara</s> in the west, <s>Rāhu</s> in the southwest, and <s>Ketu</s> in the northwest. A circle is for <s>Āditya</s>, a triangle for <s>Aṅgāraka</s>, a square for <s>Soma</s>, an arrow for <s>Budha</s>, a long rectangle for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, a pentagon for <s>Śukra</s>, a bow for <s>Śanaiścara</s>, a winnowing basket for <s>Rāhu</s>, and a banner for <s>Ketu</s>. One should know <s>Īśvara</s> as <s>Bhāskara</s>, and likewise <s>Umā</s> as <s>Soma</s>.

children.text: skandam aṅgārakaṃ caiva budho nārāyaṇaṃ sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: And <s>Skanda</s> is <s>Aṅgāraka</s>; <s>Budha</s> is established as <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.

children.text: bṛhaspatiḥ svayaṃ brahma śukraḥ śakras tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Bṛhaspati</s> is <s>Brahmā</s> himself, and <s>Śukra</s> likewise is <s>Śakra</s>.

children.text: yamaṃ śanaiścaraṃ vidyād rāhoḥ kāladūtinaḥ ketoś citraguptaś cetyete grahadevatāḥ agnir āpo bhūmir viṣṇur indrāṇī prajāpatiḥ sarpo brahmety ete pratyadhidevatāḥ jātamarka kaliṅgeṣu yāmuneṣu ca candramāḥ
children.translated_text: One should know <s>Śanaiścara</s> as <s>Yama</s>, <s>Rāhu</s> as the messenger of Time, and <s>Ketu</s> as <s>Citragupta</s>; these are the deities of the planets. <s>Agni</s>, the Waters, Earth, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Indrāṇī</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s>, the Serpent, and <s>Brahman</s>: these are the counter-deities. The Sun was born in the Arka and Kaliṅga regions, and the Moon among the Yamunas.

children.text: vindhya aṅgārakadeśo madhyadeśo budhaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: The Vindhya is the region of <s>Aṅgāraka</s>; the Middle Country is remembered as <s>Budha</s>.

children.text: bṛhaspatiḥ sindhudeśaḥ śukradeśo ghaṭeṣu ca
children.translated_text: <s>Bṛhaspati</s> is the Sindhu region, and the region of <s>Śukra</s> is among the Ghaṭas.

children.text: śanaiścaras tu saurāṣṭro rāhus tu pūrvadeśikaḥ ketuḥ parvata ity ete deśānāṃ grahajāta iti arkasamidham ādityāya pradeśamātrābhighāritānāmyādibhir juhuyāt khādiram aṅgārakāya pālāśaṃ somāyāpāmārgaṃ budhāyāśvatthaṃ bṛhaspataya audumbaraṃ śukrāya śamīṃ śanaiścarāya rāhor dūrvāḥ ketoḥ kuśāgram ity aṣṭāviṃśatim ājyāhutīr juhoty etābhiḥ pakvāgner juhoty ādityāya ilodanaṃ haviṣyam annam aṅgārakāya somāya ghṛtapāyasaṃ payodanaṃ bṛhaspataye kṣīrodanaṃ śukrāya dadhyodanaṃ budhāya tilapiṣṭamāṣodanaṃ śanaiścarāya rāhor māṃsodanaṃ ketoś citrodanam iti ā satyenety ādityāya agnir mūrdhā diva ity aṅgārakāya āpyāyasva sametu iti somāya brahma jajñānam iti budhāya bṛhaspate ati yad arya iti bṛhaspataye asya pratnām anu dyutam iti śukrāya śaṃ no devīr abhiṣṭaya iti śanaiścarāya kayā naś citra ābhuvad iti rāhoḥ ketuṃ kṛṇvann aketava iti ketoḥ raktāṃ dhenum ādityāya raktam anaḍvāham aṅgārakāya somāya śaṅkhaṃ budhāya kāñcanaṃ bṛhaspataye vāsaḥ śukrāya hayaṃ nīlāṃ gāṃ śanaiścarāya rāhoḥ kṛṣṇāyasaṃ ketoḥ kuñjaram iti sarveṣām api hiraṇyaṃ vā yena vā tuṣyaty ācāryas tad dadāti yathā samutthitaṃ yantraṃ yantreṇa pratihanyate
children.translated_text: But <s>Śanaiścara</s> is Saurāṣṭra, <s>Rāhu</s> is the eastern country, and <s>Ketu</s> is the mountain: these are the regional origins of the planets. He should offer fuel of arka wood to <s>Āditya</s>, pieces a span long and smeared with ghee, with the formulas beginning with it; khadira wood to <s>Aṅgāraka</s>, palāśa to <s>Soma</s>, apāmārga to <s>Budha</s>, aśvattha to <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, udumbara to <s>Śukra</s>, śamī to <s>Śanaiścara</s>, dūrvā grass to <s>Rāhu</s>, and the tip of kuśa grass to <s>Ketu</s>. He offers twenty-eight oblations of ghee with these. He offers from cooked fire: to <s>Āditya</s> a mess of sesame and grain as the oblation-food; to <s>Aṅgāraka</s>; to <s>Soma</s> rice pudding cooked with ghee; to <s>Bṛhaspati</s> milk-rice; to <s>Śukra</s> curd-rice; to <s>Budha</s> rice with sesame paste and māṣa beans; to <s>Śanaiścara</s>; to <s>Rāhu</s> meat-rice; and to <s>Ketu</s> variegated rice. Thus, with "By truth" for <s>Āditya</s>; "<s>Agni</s> is the head of heaven" for <s>Aṅgāraka</s>; "Increase, come together" for <s>Soma</s>; "Brahman was born" for <s>Budha</s>; "O <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, when the noble one" for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>; "Following this ancient radiance" for <s>Śukra</s>; "May the divine waters be for our help" for <s>Śanaiścara</s>; "By what wondrous one has he come to us" for <s>Rāhu</s>; and "Making a banner for the bannerless" for <s>Ketu</s>. To <s>Āditya</s> he gives a red cow; to <s>Aṅgāraka</s> a red bull; to <s>Soma</s> a conch; to <s>Budha</s> gold; to <s>Bṛhaspati</s> a garment; to <s>Śukra</s> a horse; to <s>Śanaiścara</s> a dark-blue cow; to <s>Rāhu</s> black iron; and to <s>Ketu</s> an elephant. Or, for all of them, he may give gold, or whatever satisfies the teacher. Just as a machine that has arisen is countered by a machine,

children.text: tathā grahopaspṛṣṭānāṃ śāntir bhavati dāruṇam ||
children.translated_text: so pacification comes about for those touched by the planets, even when the affliction is terrible.

children.text: nādiśet tapasā yuktaṃ nādiśed divamāśritam
children.translated_text: He should not point out one who is joined with austerity; he should not point out one who has resorted to heaven.

children.text: na ca vedāntakaṃ vipraṃ vṛttāntāṃ nārīṃ parivṛtām ||
children.translated_text: Nor should he point out a brāhmaṇa who is devoted to the end of the Veda, nor a woman who has been surrounded by events.

children.text: ahiṃsakasya dāntasya dharmajitadhanasya ca
children.translated_text: For one who is harmless, restrained, and whose wealth is won by <s>dharma</s> (righteous order),

children.text: nityaṃ ca niyamasthasya sadānugrahā grahāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and who is always established in observance, the planets are always favorable.

children.text: grahā gāvo narendrāś ca brāhmaṇāś ca viśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: Planets, cows, kings, and brāhmaṇas especially:

children.text: pūjitāḥ pūjayanty ete nirdahanty avamānitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: when honored, these honor in return; when dishonored, they burn.
